By appropriate contractions of the generalized Riemann curvature tensor, this work also provides generalizations of scalar curvature, the Ricci curvature tensor, and the Einstein tensor in any dimension.

papers.title: A Table Theorem for Surfaces with Odd Euler Characteristic
papers.abstract: We use the square peg problem for smooth curves to prove a generalized table Theorem for real valued functions on Riemannian surfaces with odd Euler characteristic. We then use this result to prove the table conjecture for even functions on the two sphere.

papers.title: A new look at unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction for toric manifolds
papers.authors: Jos\'e M. Mour\~ao, Jo\~ao P. Nunes, Augusto Pereira, Dan Wang
papers.abstract:
For a symplectic manifold $M$ with the Hamiltonian action of a compact Lie group $G$, we give a new perspective on the problem of unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence. We argue that this correspondence leads naturally to the introduction of what we call Fourier polarizations, whose real directions include the Hamiltonian vector fields of all invariant functions of the moment map.
  For a Fourier polarization, quantization commutes with reduction unitarily. For a general $G$-invariant polarization, $\mathcal{P}$, unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence can then be formulated in terms of the existence of a Fourier polarization, $\mathcal{P}_F$, such that the quantizations with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ and to $\mathcal{P}_F$ are unitarily equivalent.
  We describe this perspective in detail for symplectic toric manifolds, by considering symplectic reductions associated to the action of a subtorus $T^p\subset T^n$. We consider half-form quantization in Fourier (mixed) polarizations $\mathcal{P}_\infty$, whose real directions are generated by(the Hamiltonian vector fields of the)components of the $T^p$ moment map. We show that Fourier mixed polarizations of this type can be obtained by Mabuchi geodesic rays of toric K\"ahler structures, starting at a given initial structure and with velocity given by the norm square of the moment map of the torus subgroup.
  We lift these geodesic rays to the quantum bundle via generalized coherent state transforms, which define equivariant isomorphisms between quantum Hilbert spaces for the K\"ahler and Fourier polarizations, where the later are obtained at infinite geodesic time. Unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction in these cases then becomes equivalent to the unitarity of these isomorphisms. In general, however, in the toric case, these isomorphisms are not unitary.

papers.title: Periodic Inscription of Isosceles Trapezoids
papers.abstract: We prove that a pair of continuous disjoint periodic curves in $\mathbb{C}$ inscribes an isosceles trapezoid with any similarity type. The case of smooth curves can be identified with a Lagrangian intersection problem for a pair of Lagrangian cylinders in $\mathbb{R}\times S^1\times\mathbb{C}$, and the continuous case follows from the smooth one by a standard convergence argument.

papers.title: The truncated symbol of a differential symmetry breaking operator
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we introduce the truncated symbol of a differential symmetry breaking operator between parabolically induced representations. This generalizes the symbol map, which is defined for the case of abelian nilpotent radicals, to the non-abelian setting. The inverse of the truncated symbol map enables one to develop a recipe for the F-method for any nilpotent radical.
  As an application, we classify and construct differential intertwining operators on the full flag variety $SL(3,\mathbb{R})/B$ and homomorphisms between Verma modules. It turned out that, surprisingly, Cayley continuants appeared in the coefficients of one of the five families of operators that we constructed. At the end of the paper, factorization identities for the differential operators and homomorphisms are also classified. Binary Krawtchouk polynomials play a key role in the proof.

papers.title: Levi Flat Structures via Structure Sheaves: Differential Complexes, Convexity, and Global Solvability
papers.abstract: This paper investigates Levi flat structures from the perspective of structure sheaves. We employ formal integrability to construct a class of differential complexes, thereby providing a resolution of the structure sheaf and a global realization of the Treves complex. Drawing inspiration from Morse theory and Grauert's convexity, we introduce notions of convexity and positivity that fully exploit Levi flatness, which yield global exactness of the differential complex and Sobolev regularity in the compact case. As applications, we establish the global solvability of the Treves complex for Levi flat structures, together with results on singular cohomology and the extension problem for canonical forms in the elliptic case.

papers.title: Envelope of Holomorphy of Matsuki Orbits in Complex Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We study the envelopes of holomorphy of Matsuki orbits $M_{\ell,m,r}$ arising as intersections of $G_0$- and $K$-orbits in complex Grassmannians. These orbits, equipped with natural CR-structures, form a class of compact homogeneous CR-submanifolds whose analytic continuation properties are of fundamental interest. Building on Rossi's theory of holomorphic extension, we establish that the envelope of holomorphy of each Matsuki orbit coincides biholomorphically with the containing $K$-orbit $O_{\ell,m}$. Our approach provides a geometric proof based on the holomorphic fiber bundle structure $\pi : M_{\ell,m,r} \to \mathrm{Gr}_{\ell}(E_+) \times \mathrm{Gr}_{m}(E_-)$, clarifying the role of compact isotropic fibers in constraining holomorphic extension. Explicit examples, including the orbit $M_{1,1,1} \subset \mathrm{Gr}_3(\mathbb{C}^8)$, illustrate the method and highlight connections with classical constructions in complex geometry and representation theory.

papers.title: Zonal states and improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We establish polynomially improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces in the critical energy regime. We also show that, below the critical energy, the H\"ormander bound is saturated by explicit eigenstates, which we call magnetic zonal states. These states resemble zonal harmonics on the sphere and equidistribute on Lagrangian tori in phase space.

papers.title: Synthetic Differential Geometry in Lean
papers.abstract: This article is about the formalization of synthetic differential geometry with the Lean proof assistant and the mathematical library mathlib. The main result we prove and formalize is a Taylor theorem for functions of several variables, where the series expansion is around an infinitesimal neighborhood. Most of our proofs are in fact new. Our investigations highlight the possibility of using mathlib to do constructive mathematics.

papers.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
papers.abstract: We show that the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard disks moving freely on the plane is at least exponential in $n$.

papers.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
papers.abstract:
We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$.
  In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.

papers.title: Computing Fr\'echet Means on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fr\'echet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fr\'echet means for data supported on an unknown compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M_{1}$ embedded in an ambient metric space $(X,d_{\operatorname{obs}})$. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on $M_{1}$ and the observation metric $d_{\operatorname{obs}}$, without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an $O(1/T)$ expected objective gap guarantee using at most $\widetilde{O}(T^{4d+3})$ sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.

papers.title: Sharp Gromov Hyperbolicity Constants for Cartesian Products of Finitely Many Trees
papers.authors: Junior Michel, Anier Soria Lorente, Jean Marie-Vilaire
papers.abstract:
Let $X=T_1\times\cdots\times T_k$, $k\ge2$, be a Cartesian product of finite nontrivial trees with unit edges, and write $d_i=\diam T_i$, $S=\sum_id_i$ and $M=\max_id_i$. We prove that the thin-triangle hyperbolicity constant of the geodesic realization of $X$ is \[
  \Rips(X)=\min\Bigl\{\frac S2,\ S-M+\frac12\Bigr\}, \] and that the four-point hyperbolicity constant of its vertex metric is the value \[ \mathcal{P}(d_1,\dots,d_k) =
\max_{E\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}} \min\left\{ \sum_{i\in E} d_i,\, \sum_{i\notin E} d_i \right\}. \] of the best two-way partition of the diameters. Both constants therefore depend only on the diameter vector, and their difference is governed by the partition imbalance $\eta$ of that vector: it equals $\eta/2$ when $M\le S-M$ and $1/2$ otherwise. In particular the two constants coincide if and only if the diameters admit a perfect partition, and their difference is unbounded. For $k\ge3$ the first formula exhibits a many-factor balancing phenomenon: several short factors can collectively balance the longest one and force the universal bound $\frac12\diam X$ to be attained. The proofs are self-contained and rest on an exact distance formula for the geodesic realization of $X$. For the $\ell_1$-product of the factors, i.e.\ the $\ell_1$-metric on the associated cube complex, we obtain $\Rips=\min\{S/2,S-M\}$, which identifies the half-unit above as a pure $1$-skeleton effect, and we show that the four-point formula holds for $\ell_1$-products of arbitrary $0$-hyperbolic metric spaces, in particular for weighted trees and $\R$-trees. We also treat products with unbounded factors and record algorithmic consequences.

papers.title: Dimension Thresholds for Relative-Error Representations of Finite Metrics in Pseudo-Euclidean Spaces
papers.authors: Nikita Muravya, Aleksandr Bespalov, Anna Vozianova
papers.abstract: A finite metric space with $N$ points admits an exact representation in a pseudo-Euclidean space of dimension at most $N-1$. We study the minimum dimension required for relative-error approximation of squared distances. Our main result gives an upper bound for arbitrary metrics in terms of local distance ratios: for $4/5<\varepsilon<1$, dimension $O((N/k)\log N+k\rho_k^4\log N/(\varepsilon-4/5)^2)$ suffices, where $\rho_k$ is the largest ratio, over all points, between the distance to the $k$th closest point (counting the point itself) and the nearest-neighbour distance. The proof combines a low-rank landmark approximation with a sparse correction controlled by its factorization norm. For metrics with distances in $[1,\Phi]$, where $\Phi\ge5$ is fixed, the worst-case dimension is $\Theta(N)$ for $0<\varepsilon<4/5$, lies between $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ and $O(\sqrt N\log N)$ for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, and is $\Theta(\log N)$ for $\varepsilon>(\Phi^2-1)/(\Phi^2+1)$. For $\Phi>5$, an intermediate range remains without matching bounds. Sign-pattern counting yields the $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ lower bound for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, while Hadamard matrices give explicit linear lower bounds for $\varepsilon<4/5$ via a known approximate-rank estimate. We also construct configurations with null squared intervals whose minimum representation dimension remains $N-1$ for every $\varepsilon<1$. Finally, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<3/5$, we show that the quadratic dependence on the parameter $C$ in the dimension bound derived from Deng et al.'s pseudo-Euclidean Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is necessary up to a logarithmic factor.

papers.title: Every Extended Metric Space Is Isometrically Embeddable into the Gromov--Hausdorff Class
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{GH}$ denote the Gromov-Hausdorff class of isometry classes of nonempty metric spaces, equipped with the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, which is an extended pseudometric. We prove that every nonempty extended metric space is isometrically embeddable into $\mathfrak{GH}$. More precisely, for every nonempty extended metric space $X$, the embedding can be chosen so that all image points are represented by metrics on a common underlying set of cardinality $\max\{\mathrm{dens}\,X,\aleph_0\}$, where $\mathrm{dens}\,X$ denotes the density character of $X$. To establish this result, for every nonempty set $I$, we realize the space of all real-valued functions on $I$, equipped with the uniform extended metric, as a family of metrics on a fixed underlying set. Under this realization, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance agrees with the uniform extended distance between functions, including when this distance is infinite, and each resulting metric space is complete, uniformly discrete, and unbounded, with cardinality $\max\{|I|,\aleph_0\}$. When $I$ is countable, the representing spaces can also be chosen proper and of bounded geometry. We also show that, for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$, there are exactly $2^\kappa$ clouds represented by metric spaces of cardinality at most $\kappa$, and that $2^\kappa$ of their cardinality-restricted parts are isometrically universal for all metric spaces of density character at most $\kappa$. Furthermore, every sphere of positive radius centered at a point of the constructed copies of $\ell^\infty(\kappa)$ in the zero-distance quotients admits isometric embeddings of all metric spaces of density character at most $\kappa$ and diameter at most twice the radius.

papers.title: Infinitesimally Euclidean metric surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove the equivalence of several notions of infinitesimally Euclidean-like behaviour for metric surfaces appearing in the literature. We obtain in particular that metric surfaces with property (ET) are universally infinitesimally Hilbertian.

papers.title: Distributions of metric $n$-point invariants and applications to molecular evolution
papers.authors: Michael Bleher, Mario G\'omez, Facundo M\'emoli, Maximilian Neumann, Andreas Ott
papers.abstract: Datasets often arise as samples from a metric measure space whose geometry reflects the data-generating process. We introduce metric $n$-point invariants, defined as functions of the pairwise distances of $n$-point configurations, to study the geometry of such spaces. This provides a unified framework for existing concepts, such as the pairwise distance itself, the Gromov product, and Vietoris-Rips persistence diagrams. The distribution of a metric $n$-point invariant $F$ over random $n$-point configurations can be used to extract geometric information from the space and is obtained as the pushforward of Gromov's $n$-th curvature measure $\mu_n$ along $F$. Our main result is an explicit bound for the expected $p$-Wasserstein distance between $\mu_n$ and the empirical curvature measure $\hat{\mu}_{n}$ of finitely many sampled $n$-point configurations, and carries over to the associated distributions of Lipschitz metric $n$-point invariants. From this we derive the sample size needed to achieve a prescribed accuracy and level of confidence in the approximation of the curvature measure. As an application, we use metric $n$-point invariants to study molecular evolution. We describe how site-wise nucleotide frequencies shape the corresponding distributions in Jukes-Cantor and Halpern-Bruno substitution models, and analyse five million SARS-CoV-2 genomes, revealing increasingly common failures of the four-point condition, constrained nucleotide accessibility consistent with the biased mutation spectrum, and rare cycles in persistent homology reflecting recurrent mutations across lineages. These findings demonstrate the potential of our sampling-based approach to the geometry of data as a scalable, phylogeny-free tool for detecting and quantifying evolutionary structure in large genomic datasets.

papers.title: Depth based on translates of a convex body: geometry, floating bodies, and empirical theory
papers.abstract: For a fixed full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, we study the $K$-depth of a point $y$ with respect to a probability measure $\mu$ by comparing the masses of translates of $K$ that fail to contain $y$. Its upper level sets are intersections of high-mass translates of $K$, and hence are convex and admit an exact representation as Minkowski erosions. We distinguish the closed core determined by the maximisers of the translation-mass function from the effective support on which the depth exceeds its unavoidable baseline. We establish continuity, affine equivariance, comparison with halfspace (Tukey) depth, and normal-cone and smoothness criteria. For uniform measures on convex bodies, the regions coincide exactly with the ball floating bodies of Sch\"utt, Werner and Yalikun; for positive continuous densities they coincide with the weighted ball floating bodies of Werner and Yalikun. For dilates $tK$, the depth converges to a depth generated by the tangent cones of $K$ as $t \to \infty$; for smooth $K$ this limit is Tukey's halfspace depth, whereas nonsmooth testing bodies can produce a genuinely different limit. The worst-case maximal $K$-depth is exactly $1/h_T(K)$, where $h_T(K)$ is the Helly number of the family of translates of $K$. Under a uniform interior rolling-ball condition and compact support and having zero mass on hyperplanes, the convergence to halfspace depth is monotone and uniform with an explicit error bound. If the density is bounded by $L$, then this bound is of order $O(t^{-1})$ and this order is sharp. We also record that the dependence on the testing body is not monotone in general, while Hausdorff perturbations of $K$ give stable depth functions and regions at regular levels. Finally, we prove uniform consistency and pointwise weak limits for empirical $K$-depth, including the non-Gaussian limit caused by nonunique active translates.

papers.title: Finite convexification by Minkowski summation
papers.abstract: Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact set and let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact convex set. We study the problem of when there exists $\lambda>0$ such that the Minkowski sum $A+\lambda K$ is convex. First, we show that this finite convexification is equivalent to a uniform covering condition on the exposed sets of $A$ and $K$. We then show that another characterization is possible in terms of the covering radii of the iterated exposed sets after translating each exposed face of $K$ so that its relative centroid is $0$. In the case of convex polytopes, we show that it suffices to check the exposed sets in the first level of the iteration. We also study several special cases, such as strictly convex convexifiers, lower-dimensional convexifiers, strongly isomorphic polytopes, and the planar case.

papers.title: Diamond Maximal Operators: Classification, Moduli, and Oscillation Envelopes
papers.abstract: We study maximal averages generated by bounded cancellative kernels taking values in finite-dimensional real normed spaces, on Euclidean balls and on balls in a non-Archimedean local field with a fixed uniformizer. For angular kernels, pointwise domination of the full maximal operators is equivalent to factorization of their angular averaging maps, with the same optimal constant. Nonzero scalar angular comparison classes are therefore projective kernel classes. For angular kernels constant on a fixed finite measurable partition of the direction space, symmetric convex bodies classify exact norm measurements, Grassmannians parametrize nonzero classes under mutual domination, and positive semidefinite Gram matrices classify Hilbert-valued measurements. For general kernels, the closed convex hull of the averaging densities obtained from all scales and the dual unit ball is a complete invariant of the full maximal operator. A dilation example exhibits identifications of residue kernels beyond scaling and unit-coordinate changes. For nonzero radial residue kernels on bounded inputs, mutual domination is classified by the unit-circle zeros of filter polynomials, counted with multiplicity, with optimal constants given by the $\ell^1$ norms of convolution quotients. We identify the envelope over all normalized bounded cancellative kernels with the best local $L^1$ approximation by constants and prove quantitative convergence of residue envelopes as the resolution increases. Finally, the weights of the finite Fourier transform classify the one-level energy and the associated Carleson functional. This functional is equivalent to the $BMO_2$ seminorm precisely when every nontrivial additive character of the residue field is detected, and the weights determine the optimal comparison constants.

papers.title: Thompson's groups are sofic
papers.authors: Maksym Chaudkhari, Kate Juschenko, Kyrylo Muliarchyk
papers.abstract: We prove that Thompson's groups $F$, $T$ and $V$ are sofic. As a corollary, all of them are also hyperlinear and not permutation stable. The proof relies on an explicit construction of sofic approximations to $F$ and $V$. Moreover, the construction allows us to obtain effective quantitative bounds on the parameters of sofic approximations.

papers.title: Geometric and measure-theoretic characterizations of the measure-determining property of balls in metric spaces
papers.abstract: The question of what structural properties drive the collection of open or closed balls to uniquely determine Borel probability measures on a metric space, the ball property, has a long history in measure theory. While various sufficient conditions have been known since the 1970s, and it was shown by Preiss and Ti\v{s}er (1991) that it holds for all separable Banach spaces, Davies (1971) constructed a famous counterexample that shows it can fail on compact metric spaces. It was only recently established in van Delft (2026) that metric spaces admitting an isometric Hilbertian embedding must possess the ball property. This article provides a comprehensive structural and measure-theoretic characterization of the ball property. First, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the ball property to fail: the collection of balls must possess sufficient combinatorial capacity, which we define as charged dyadic shattering. Second, by characterizing the ball property via $\lambda$-systems, we place classical vector space results within a unified context. Building on this to understand spaces that have the topological capacity but lack linear or geometric rigidity required to force ball-annihilating measures to zero, we relate the metric outer measure to the cylinder outer measure on countable products of Polish spaces, deriving necessary and sufficient measure-theoretic conditions for the ball property to hold. This allows us to derive a structural taxonomy on the decoupling of the metric outer measure from the cylinder outer measure. This is subsequently used to deconstruct Davies' counterexample. Finally, we introduce a minimal combinatorial generalization of the ball property, the $n$th order ball property, and show that such classes can fully recover measure determination in highly pathological constructions like Davies' counterexample.

papers.title: Union of Translates of a Convex Body
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of calculating the volume of the union of translates of a strictly convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. When $K$ is a ball, it is possible to simplify the inclusion-exclusion formula by summing over only a small subset of all terms. This subset corresponds to intersecting cells in the Voronoi diagram of the ball centers. We prove that the same simplification is valid for every strictly convex $K$ if and only if $d\leq 2$. Moreover, in three dimensions and when $K$ is $C^4$, we use the Fubini-Pick affine invariant to show that the topological identity underlying this technique holds if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid.

papers.title: Local structure of sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets
papers.abstract: We show that if $X$ and $Y$ are self-similar sets in $\mathbb{R}$ with multiplicatively independent contraction ratios, then the Assouad dimension of $X+Y$ is one. As an application, we show that for a large class of self-affine carpets, the Assouad dimension of any non-principal orthogonal projection is one. The latter result is new even for the simplest case of Bedford-McMullen carpets.

papers.title: Counting Lattice Points in Translations: Uniqueness and Existence Results
papers.abstract: Generalizing a recent theorem by Higashitani et al. (Comb. Theory 2025), it is shown that a convex body $K$ is uniquely described up to integer translation by the function $\mathrm{t}_K(v) = |(K-v)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n|$, $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$. For a lattice polytope $P$ the function $\mathrm{t}_P$ is decomposed into homogeneous components $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$, similar to the Ehrhart polynomial. It is shown that the functions $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$ are simultaneous eigenfunctions of a family of linear operators introduced by Kubert and Lang in (Math. Z. 1976) and that, conversely, the linear spaces of piecewise constant eigenfunctions are generated by the respective coefficients $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$. A structure theorem for the simultaneous eigenspace corresponding to the $(n-1)$st coefficient in the decomposition of $\mathrm{t}_P$ is obtained. This leads to an explicit description of the set of functions $\mathrm{t}_P$, where $P$ ranges over all lattice polygons, as well as to inequalities for the number of lattice points in dilated and translated lattice polytopes.

papers.title: On the uniqueness of $p$-energy on the Sierpi\'nski carpet
papers.abstract: For any $p\in(1,+\infty)$, it is proved that the self-similar $p$-energy on the Sierpi\'nski carpet is unique, up to multiplication by a positive constant.

papers.title: The moduli space of quasimorphisms on subshifts and its pressure geometry
papers.authors: Stephen Cantrell, Pablo Carrasco, Emilio Corso, Federico Rodriguez Hertz
papers.abstract: We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are $C^1$, with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for H\"older potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.

papers.title: Asymptotics of Constrained Quantization for Compactly Supported Measures
papers.abstract:
We study constrained quantization of a compactly supported probability $P$ on $\mathbb{R}^D$ by codebooks in a nonempty closed set $S$. For $0<r\le\infty$, the constrained error $e_{n,r}$ is attained and satisfies $e_{n,r}\downarrow L_r=\|\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,S)\|_{L^r(P)}$. Set $\Delta_{n,r}=e_{n,r}^r-L_r^r$ for finite $r$. A Borel nearest-point selector $T$ induces $\mu=T_*P$. Writing $q_{n,s}$ for the classical $L^s$ quantization error, we obtain $e_{n,r}-L_r\le2q_{n,r}(\mu)$ and $\Delta_{n,r}\le C_rq_{n,1}(\mu)$ for $1\le r<\infty$, with $C_r$ independent of $n$, and $\Delta_{n,r}\le2^rq_{n,r}(\mu)^r$ for $0<r<1$. Also, $e_{n,\infty}-L_\infty\le2c_n(E)$, where $E$ is the nearest-point image of $\operatorname{supp}P$ and $c_n(E)$ is its covering radius. For $1\le r<\infty$, a weighted power-growth condition with exponent $ eta>0$ on a fixed source set $F$ bounds $\Delta_{n,r}$ below by the classical $ eta$-power quantization cost of $
u_F=T_*(wP|_F)$. If $d
u_F=\widehat w\,d\eta$ for a compactly supported reference probability $\eta$ and $\widehat w\in A_p(\eta)$, $1<p<\infty$, then $\Delta_{n,r}\ge
u_F(\mathbb{R}^D)[\widehat w]_{A_p(\eta)}^{-1}q_{n, eta/p}(\eta)^ eta$. These comparisons yield bounds for the quantization dimensions defined by $e_{n,r}-L_r$ and $\Delta_{n,r}^{1/r}$, with distinct behavior at positive and zero baselines. Convex and uniformly prox-regular constraints supply the growth weights through their projection inequalities. Circle and lifted Cantor distributions give matching quadratic-excess rates, while rectifiable weighted projections give lower Zador estimates.

papers.title: Notes on uniform contractions of congruent balls
papers.abstract: In this note, we obtain stronger results on uniform contractions of intersections and unions of congruent balls, thereby extending previous partial confirmations of the Kneser-Poulsen conjecture in these settings. In addition, we establish Blaschke-Santal\'o-type inequalities for r-ball bodies.

papers.title: Tiling a triangle into a prime number of congruent triangles
papers.abstract:
We prove that if a triangle is cut into $N$ congruent triangles and $N$ is prime, then $N=2$, $N=3$, or $N\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, and every such $N$ occurs. In particular, if $N > 3$ then $N$ is not a prime congruent to $3$ modulo $4$.
  The argument divides into cases according to possible shapes of the tiled triangle. Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the angles of the tile. Prior to this posting, there remained several open shapes. The two most difficult shapes were $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, the {\em triquadratic} shape, and $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha)$, the {\em isosceles-$\beta$} shape, in which $3\alpha+2\beta = \pi$ and $\alpha$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi$. A previous version of this paper relied on incorrect proofs of those cases, which have been retracted, and are replaced here by correct proofs. For each of those two shapes the number of tiles has the form $N = j^2 N_0$, where $N_0 > 1$ is determined by the shape of the tile and $j$ is a positive integer; so $N$ is prime, or even squarefree, only if $j = 1$. We prove by geometric reasoning that neither shape admits a tiling with $j = 1$, which shows that for both shapes $N$ is never prime, and indeed never squarefree.
  The shape $(\beta,\beta,3\alpha+\beta)$ (where $3\alpha + 3\beta = \pi$) has been settled by Bonfioli. In this paper, we settle the remaining cases, by number-theoretic arguments based on the area equation. Those proofs rule out $N$ prime, but not $N$ squarefree, and we give examples to show that tilings with squarefree $N$ do sometimes exist.

papers.title: Pyramidal Compactification of Asymmetric Metric Measure Spaces via Adjoint Transport
papers.abstract: A quasi-metric measure space (qm-space) is a set with a directed distance whose symmetrization is a complete separable metric, together with a Borel probability measure of full support. Motivated by the problem of determining the pyramid limits of beta measures on forward Funk balls, we construct a compact metric space of pyramids of qm-spaces. The associated-pyramid map from the concentration-distance space of qm-spaces into this compact space is a $1$-Lipschitz topological embedding with dense image. As a secondary result, we prove that the box-distance space of qm-spaces is complete and separable.

papers.title: On the Log-submodularity for zonoids: from Mixed Volume inequalities to the Hypercube
papers.authors: Gennadiy Averkov, Katherina von Dichter, Ivan Soprunov
papers.abstract: In convex geometry, a number of inequalities for the volume of coordinate projections of convex bodies share a common structural property. We formalize them as inequalities of log-submodularity type, providing a definition that stems from the notion of a submodular function. The Loomis-Whitney inequality and some of its generalizations are the most prominent examples. Some inequalities of log-submodularity type are valid for zonoids but not for general convex bodies. They have a natural meaning in statistics and information theory. We propose a new inequality of log-submodularity type for zonoids. In dimension 3, our inequality is equivalent to the log-submodularity conjecture for zonoids formulated by Fradelizi, Madiman, Meyer, and Zvavitch, which is true in dimension $3$ and false in higher dimensions. In contrast, our inequality is true in every dimension. We reduce our inequality to copositivity of a special polynomial, which we call the hypercube polynomial. For 4-dimensional zonoids, we verify the copositivity of the respective hypercube polynomial algebraically by providing a sum-of-squares certificate. In every dimension, a proof of copositivity of the hypercube polynomial that uses probability theory and well-known matrix inequalities has been produced by LLMs and brought to our attention. We present a detailed and easy-to-read version of this proof.

papers.title: The Spherical Hadwiger Theorem
papers.abstract: We prove the spherical Hadwiger theorem in every dimension: for $n\geq1$, every continuous $\mathrm{SO}(n+1)$-invariant valuation on all closed spherical convex sets in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ is a unique linear combination of the spherical intrinsic volumes $V_0,\ldots,V_n$. The same classification holds on sets contained in an open hemisphere, with unique continuous invariant extension to the full domain. We first classify simple invariant valuations by an independent induction on dimension. Averaging a signed cone identity gives the spherical volume term; the remaining terms are signed coning transforms that vanish by the lower-dimensional simple classification. A second induction, together with extension to non-proper sets, gives the general classification. The cone--sphere correspondence yields, for $d\geq2$, the corresponding classification on all closed convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without normalization at the zero cone. In both settings, $\mathrm{SO}$-invariance implies $\mathrm{O}$-invariance.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff Distances Between Spheres: Asymptotics and Vietoris-Rips Coindex Bounds
papers.authors: Sunhyuk Lim, Facundo M\'emoli, Qingsong Wang
papers.abstract: For $1\le m<n$, let $c_{m,n}$ be the infimum of the scales $r$ at which the Vietoris-Rips simplicial complex of the unit round sphere $\mathbb{S}^m$, equipped with its geodesic metric, admits a continuous odd map from $\mathbb{S}^n$. Previous work established the lower bound $\frac{1}{2}c_{m,n}\le d_{\mathrm{GH}}(\mathbb{S}^m,\mathbb{S}^n)$ through a quantitative Borsuk-Ulam theorem and raised the question of whether it is always sharp. We show that this bound can underestimate the distance by a factor arbitrarily close to two, the largest possible factor. Combining projective-code upper bounds for $c_{m,n}$ with lower bounds for $d_{\mathrm{GH}}$ obtained from obstructions to homomorphisms between Borsuk graphs, we obtain explicit finite-dimensional bounds. Along sequences of pairs $1\le m<n$, we have $c_{m,n}\to\frac{\pi}{2}$ whenever $\log n/m\to0$, while $d_{\mathrm{GH}}(\mathbb{S}^m,\mathbb{S}^n)\to\frac{\pi}{2}$ whenever $m/n\to0$. When both conditions hold (for example when $n=m^2$) the ratio of the distance to $\frac{1}{2}c_{m,n}$ tends to two. For each fixed $m\ge3$, the inequality is strict for all sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: Exponential improvements in Rado's covering problem
papers.abstract:
Let $B^d$ denote the $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball of unit radius. What is the largest constant $f(B^d) \in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $f(B^d)$ of the volume of $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T. Rad\'o in 1928, for axis-parallel squares in the plane; the author was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. The case of Euclidean balls was first considered by R. Rado in 1949.
  Until last year the best known estimates on $f(B^d)$ for unit balls where very far apart: \[ (1+\epsilon_d) 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2^{-d}, \] where $0<\epsilon_d=o_{d\rightarrow \infty}(1)$. Recently, the authors of this note observed that an exponential improvement on the upper bound follows from the Kabatiansky--Levenshtein spherical code bound, while the lower bound was improved by a linear factor by C.~Xie and G.~Ge (see arxiv:2608.09744). The current best estimates for large $d$ are \[ c \cdot d \cdot 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}, \] where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. Here we offer the first exponential improvement of the lower bound in almost 80 years, which narrows the gap to:
  \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}. \] Our method is constructive and yields a polynomial time algorithm for finding a disjoint sub-collection realizing the estimate. Moreover the same technique gives similar exponentially improved lower bounds for all symmetric convex bodies satisfying a uniform convexity assumption, e.g., $\ell^p$-balls for all $p\in (1,\infty)$.

papers.title: The packing spectrum: interpolation between Hausdorff and packing dimensions
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of metric outer measures whose critical exponents form a packing spectrum interpolating between Hausdorff and packing dimensions. For analytic sets, we characterize each spectral value as the supremum of the Hausdorff dimension of a product with a compact testing set minus the testing set's upper intermediate dimension at the complementary parameter. The associated product bounds refine the classical Hausdorff--packing inequalities and can give exact Hausdorff additivity when both factors have distinct endpoint dimensions. Below the packing endpoint, we prove a variational principle in terms of windowed local mass exponents and sharp parameter estimates implying local Lipschitz continuity; a jump at the endpoint is possible. We characterize all attainable profiles by monotonicity, continuity below the packing endpoint, and a sharp upper right Dini-derivative bound. Every admissible profile is realized by a compact binary digit set whose uniform measure attains the finite-window and classical packing variational suprema. Complementary digit positions yield reflected upper intermediate-dimension profiles and a single factor attaining the Hausdorff product bounds at every parameter, with an Ahlfors regular product measure.

papers.title: Semidefinite programming bounds for distance distribution of spherical codes
papers.abstract: Multipoint semidefinite programming bounds for spherical codes use polynomials in several variables. We show how to obtain bounds for the distance distribution using a polynomial of one variable on a prescribed interval. The multivariate SDP supplies the required positivity; the sign and size of the univariate polynomial reveal the geometric consequences. We prove three- and four-point reductions and explain how to choose the polynomial to bound the number of pairs in a prescribed interval. Three-point experiments in dimension four illustrate this procedure, including nearly antipodal pairs, intervals near inner product $1/2$, and a local approach to the kissing number bound. As a further application, we extract a degree-six polynomial from the exact four-point construction of de Laat, Leijenhorst, and de Muinck Keizer. Its sign and four zeros give a direct description of the distance restriction underlying uniqueness of the $24$-cell.

papers.title: Topological and Diophantine properties of lattice subset projections
papers.abstract: This paper uses the Baire category theorem, the Riemannian manifold structure of Grassmannians, and the Khintchine Groshev theorem in Diophantine analysis, to relate properties of lattice subsets to those of associated subset of a Grassmannian.

papers.title: The Geometry of Anisotropic Dilation for Optimal Regularization
papers.abstract: How can structured transformations of data improve regularizer design for inverse problems? We address this question through anisotropic dilation, a direction-preserving map that rescales each point along its Euclidean ray by a positive profile on the sphere. Our analysis builds on a characterization of optimal regularizers within a broad Gibbs class, where the regularizer best matched to a distribution $P$ is determined by a direction-dependent radial summary statistic $\rho_P$. We show that anisotropic dilation acts explicitly and transitively on the space of radial summary statistics: any prescribed optimal regularizer in this class can be obtained by transforming an admissible source distribution using a single explicit profile. We characterize the resulting distributional orbits and establish conditions under which this control of regularizer geometry yields a weakly convex denoising formulation even when the original objective is not weakly convex. We also derive in closed form the profile that optimally adapts a fixed base regularizer to data. Its improvement over isotropic rescaling with respect to KL divergence is governed by a Jensen gap, for which we establish strict positivity under explicit conditions for several natural families of distributions. For jointly learning the base regularizer and anisotropic profile from samples, we establish finite-sample generalization bounds, with explicit rates when the logarithm of the profile is parameterized by linear feature models or sparse ReLU networks. Experiments on a controlled two-dimensional family and on MNIST denoising demonstrate that learning the anisotropic profile can improve reconstruction performance for both handcrafted and learned base regularizers.

papers.title: Explicit formula for the Rasmussen invariant of odd pretzel knots
papers.abstract: We compute the Rasmussen s-invariant for all odd pretzel knots, giving an explicit closed formula. The formula extends to all slice-torus invariants that are invariant under mutation. In the absence of mutation invariance, we prove the formula under a mild condition on the pretzel parameters, which we conjecture to be unnecessary.

papers.title: Finiteness of Anosov and pseudo-Anosov flows on hyperbolic 3-manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that for any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$, there are only finitely many Anosov or pseudo-Anosov flows on $M$ up to orbit equivalence.

papers.title: On the kissing number of hyperbolic surfaces with a small systole
papers.abstract:
Parlier proved that there exists a constant $U>0$ such that for any hyperbolic surface $S$ of genus $g$ with systole $\ell$ the following holds: \[ Kiss(S)\leq U \frac {e^\ell}\ell g \] where $Kiss(S)$ is the maximum number of homotopically distinct systoles in $S$ (Kissing number).
  We show that there exists a constant $V>0$ and a sequence $S_n$ of hyperbolic homogeneous surfaces of genus $g_n\to \infty$ with a bounded systole such that \[ Kiss(S_n)\geq Vg_n \] for all $n\geq 1$. This shows that Parlier's theorem is sharp for a fixed systole length.
  Our proof uses Bruhat--Tits buildings of type $\tilde A_2$ and Hamiltonian surfaces.

papers.title: Analytic quantum invariants
papers.authors: Rinat Kashaev, Vladimir Mangazeev, Marcos Marino
papers.abstract: Using a deformed Borel-Laplace resummation, we propose a framework for repackaging quantum invariants as analytic invariants. We illustrate our approach through a detailed analysis of the coloured Jones polynomials of several simple knots, deriving explicit expressions for the resulting analytic invariants in terms of $(q,X)$-series. These invariants are closely related to, but generally distinct from, those obtained via the conventional Borel resummation of the Melvin-Morton-Rozansky expansion. As a further example, we construct an analytic invariant from a sequence of two-variable polynomials conjectured to be the Links-Gould polynomials of the figure-eight knot, associated with the quantum superalgebras $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}(n|1))$. Finally, we apply our technique to $q$-series arising in the study of three-manifold invariants, revealing connections with mock modular forms.

papers.title: Density of length ratios on Teichm\"uller space
papers.abstract: We study length ratios of simple closed geodesics on finite-type hyperbolic surfaces of positive genus. We allow cusps and fix the geodesic boundary lengths. Let $d$ be the dimension of the corresponding Teichm\"uller space $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{L}}(S)$. We prove that for every positive vector $(r_0,\ldots,r_d)$, the set of surfaces carrying $d+1$ distinct essential interior simple closed geodesics with lengths proportional to this vector is dense in $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{L}}(S)$. In particular, one-holed tori with three distinct simple closed geodesics of equal length are dense. The proof uses high powers of Dehn twists, asymptotics of length differentials, and the Brouwer fixed-point theorem.

papers.title: Stein fillable contact structures with half Giroux torsion
papers.abstract: We show that there exist Stein fillable contact 3-manifolds which contain a separating half Giroux torsion layer. Our examples are on Seifert fibred spaces over the sphere.

papers.title: A counterexample to the geometric triangulation conjecture of Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio
papers.abstract: Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio conjectured that an ideal triangulation in which every edge has valence at least six can be realized by hyperbolic partially truncated tetrahedra on the compact manifold it defines. We show that this is false. Starting from the figure-eight knot complement, we construct a triangulation with $2688$ tetrahedra and edge valences six and eighteen whose manifold is hyperbolic with totally geodesic boundary, but which admits no such realization. The obstruction is a critical point of the covolume energy of Luo and Yang at which three tetrahedra have collapsed: convexity then excludes every geometric competitor, an Euler characteristic count excludes edges of length zero, and the critical point itself is located by a finite certificate in exact integer arithmetic. The obstruction persists in every finite cover, while a complementary theorem shows that no counterexample can have only two edge lengths or only two orbits of edges.

papers.title: Negative-Definite Plumbings and New Unknotting Numbers
papers.abstract: We use Neumann's normal form to decide whether the double branched cover of a knot bounds a negative-definite plumbing tree in either orientation, starting from the recognised Seifert or graph-manifold structure of the cover. For many non-alternating knots with at most thirteen crossings whose unknotting numbers were unknown, this identifies the cases in which the Heegaard Floer homology of the cover can be computed from such a plumbing, and shows for most of the others that it cannot. We determine 112 new unknotting numbers. For 43 of them, the lower bound rests on Heegaard Floer homology computed from the plumbing; for the other 69, it comes from linking pairings and from a theorem of McCoy and Park on special alternating knots. Finally, we show that the knot 13n1587 is a further explicit counterexample to the Bernhard--Jablan conjecture, after 13n3370.

papers.title: Biquandle Image Quivers
papers.authors: Geunyoung Kim, Sam Nelson, Puttipong Pongtanapaisan
papers.abstract: We introduce a new family of weighted quiver-valued invariants of oriented classical and virtual knots and link, surface-knots and surface-links, and immersed surface-knots and surface-links associated to finite biquandles. We derive several polynomial invariants from these quivers via decategorification. We provide examples to illustrate the computation of the invariant as well as toy examples showing tables of invariant values for small biquandles.

papers.title: Which Immersions into Euclidean Space are Boundary Immersions?
papers.abstract: Here we study the problem of whether a given codimension one immersion $f$ of a closed and connected manifold into Euclidean space can be extended to an equidimensional immersion $F$ of some compact manifold $M$ whose restriction to the boundary parameterizes the image $S$ of $f$. Such an extension $F$ exists if and only if (i) simple conditions on orientations and wrapping numbers are satisfied and (ii) a distinguished finite subset of the first cohomology of $S$ with coefficients in a certain sheaf of finite groups contains the preferred point.

papers.title: Non-planar contact structures with Calabi-Yau Fillings and topological quantum computation
papers.abstract: This paper is a non-planar counterpart of the author's earlier work on planar contact structures and topological quantum computation. There the page is planar and all branch points are paired by disjoint liftable arcs, compatibly with the joint eigenlines of the Ising representation and with Calabi-Yau (CY) Stein fillings, those with vanishing first Chern class. Here the page has genus g and connected binding, presented as a simple degree-three cover of the disk. Every maximal system of disjoint liftable arcs has exactly g members and leaves two branch points unused. The half-twist interchanging the two points is not liftable, but its cube is, and lifts to the identity. An integral residue criterion supplies the CY test. A factorization localized on a contact connected sum is automatically CY. Unlike in the planar case, a CY factorization need not be the shortest. Once the fusion channels of the g pairs are fixed, Ising fusion determines the channel of the remaining pair, and braiding acts there only by scalars. Fibonacci fusion can leave that channel undetermined, and the powers of the cube then act by ten distinct relative phases on a single joint eigenspace, while the CY Stein filling stays fixed

papers.title: Topological mapping class groups of non-simply connected 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct topological isotopy invariants of homeomorphisms of non-simply connected 4-manifolds using the topological Dax invariant of disks and the Freedman-Quinn invariant of spheres. Our invariants are effective for various non-smoothable 4-manifolds without assuming that the fundamental groups are good. They detect infinite-rank free abelian direct factors of the pseudoisotopy-trivial and homotopy-trivial mapping class groups, and give lower bounds on the Pr\"ufer rank of the Torelli groups modulo homotopy-trivial mapping classes, including examples of infinite Pr\"ufer rank. Our method is also useful for smooth 4-manifolds. We construct stably smoothable homeomorphisms of the Enriques surface and many Dolgachev surfaces that act trivially on homology but are not homotopic to the identity.

papers.title: The Structure of the Ghost and Swapping Algebras
papers.abstract: The swapping algebras and the ghost algebras were introduced in the papers of Labourie and Bridgeman--Labourie to encode the Poisson structure on spaces of length functions and generalized cross-ratio functions associated to $\Theta$-Anosov representations. They used these algebras to show that correlation functions are stable under the Poisson bracket associated to Atiyah-Bott-Goldman's symplectic form and that length functions are convex along the Hamiltonian flow of other length functions. In this paper, we study the algebraic relationship between these two algebras. In particular, we show that the kernel of a natural surjection from the ghost algebra onto the extended swapping algebra is generated by five families of relations. Consequently, we obtain an isomorphism from an explicit quotient of the ghost algebra onto the extended swapping algebra.

papers.title: Uniform convergence of canonical discrete uniformization on equilateral approximations
papers.abstract: We prove uniform convergence of the canonical discrete uniformization maps for every sequence of equilateral polygonal disks whose mesh tends to zero and whose marked Jordan boundaries converge uniformly. The limit is the normalized Riemann map, with convergence on the entire closed reference triangle. This proves Conjecture 7.3 of Luo, Sun and Wu for the original construction with Delaunay flips. The proof combines closed-domain compactness, marked lattice limits, a packing and resistance estimate for logarithmic cusp scales, and an envelope comparison principle, followed by a local affine energy argument.

papers.title: Asymptotics for the number of saddle connections on a slit torus
papers.abstract: We consider a flat torus with a marked line segment $\beta$ and prove linear asymptotics for closed curves on the torus disjoint from the interior of the line segment. We also consider segments that begin and terminate at the end points of $\beta$ whose interiors are disjoint from $\beta$ and prove $L\log L$ asymptotics. In all cases, after quotienting by the growth rate, we compute the constant explicitly, which differs depending on whether or not $\beta$ lies in a periodic direction on the torus. In particular, when $\beta$ lies along a non-periodic trajectory, we show the constant is $2/(|\beta| \zeta(2))$. Moreover, we prove that as a function of the holonomy vector of $\beta$, the constants are continuous at the points where $\beta$ lies in a non-periodic direction.

papers.title: The minimum number of vertices of a triangulation of $\mathbb{RP}^5$
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that every finite simplicial triangulation of real projective five-space has at least twenty-four vertices. Together with the construction of Guyer, Steinerberger, and Yang, this determines the minimum. A cup-product argument produces an induced subcomplex on sixteen or seventeen vertices. Transfer to the spherical double cover then imposes a covering condition on its lifted faces. In the sixteen-vertex case, a direct capacity bound excludes twenty-two vertices. For twenty-three vertices, a cochain extension argument reduces every relevant completion to one of 115 critical signed complexes; integer weights and exact covering certificates exclude all of them. The argument requires no assumption that the triangulation is combinatorial.

papers.title: Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures
papers.abstract: We study the geography of taut foliations on compact $3$-manifolds with toroidal boundary components. The central object of our work is the set of boundary multislopes realized by foliations transverse to a fixed flow on such a manifold. We prove that these sets exhibit remarkable structural properties (rationality, rigidity, and convexity) which motivate the name ziggurats. Our main tool, of independent interest, is a two-way correspondence between foliations and contact structures on $3$-manifolds with boundary: we generalize the Eliashberg-Thurston theorem, which produces pairs of positive and negative contact structures from foliations, and a construction of the first author, which builds foliations from such contact pairs. Using both directions of this correspondence, we bring contact-geometric methods to bear on the architecture of ziggurats.

papers.title: Biquandle-Based Invariants of Virtual Knotoids and Connected Sum
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the behavior of biquandle-based invariants of virtual knotoids under their connected sum. We first show that the fundamental biquandle of the connected sum of two virtual knotoids is the pushout of a span in the category of biquandles. By applying the Hom functor to this pushout description, we obtain the correspondence between biquandle colorings of $K_1 \# K_2$ and compatible pairs of colorings of summands. This provides a categorical explanation of a known matrix product formula for biquandle counting matrices under connected sum. We then study the behavior of biquandle virtual bracket invariants under connected sum. We introduce normalized multiset invariants derived from biquandle virtual brackets and show that they are strictly stronger than their unnormalized versions in certain cases by an explicit example. Furthermore, we show that for each coloring of the connected sum $K_1 \# K_2$ corresponding to a compatible pair of colorings of the summands $K_1$ and $K_2$, the normalized biquandle virtual bracket value factors as the product of the normalized values of the summands. Building on this, we obtain connected-sum formulas for the normalized multiset invariants defined by utilizing biquandle virtual brackets. When the coefficient ring is a number ring, the normalized bracket multisets can be encoded by polynomials and matrices with polynomial entries. We introduce an induced matrix product $\odot$ and show that the normalized biquandle virtual bracket matrices satisfy \begin{equation} \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_1 \# K_2) = \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_1) \odot \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_2). \end{equation}

papers.title: Lens spaces that cannot be obtained by two integral surgeries
papers.abstract: In this article, we demonstrate that there exists an infinite family of lens spaces L(p,q) that cannot be obtained from the 3-sphere by two integral surgeries. The first such lens space in our family is L(177,29).

papers.title: Computing the Hopf invariant
papers.abstract: We consider Whitehead's integral formula and propose an algorithm for computing the Hopf invariant for simplicial mappings.

papers.title: Chow Vanishing and Motives of Cluster Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that the integral Chow groups $CH_i$ and mixed Hodge degree $H^{2i, (i, i)}$ cohomology groups of a really full rank (RFR) sink-recurrent cluster variety vanish for $i > 0$. In particular this applies to braid varieties and open projected Richardson varieties in any Lie type. Our main technical tool is the construction of a stratification of any RFR sink-recurrent cluster variety $\mathcal{A}(\Sigma)$ over any field $k$ into (affine space times) RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties of seeds with fewer mutable vertices than $\Sigma$, with which we show that RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties are linear in the sense of Totaro. We also show that cycle class maps are isomorphisms onto the lowest-weight part of rational Borel-Moore homology for any mixed Tate variety over a number field. Finally, we use our results to deduce vanishing theorems for the Khovanov-Rozansky homology groups of closures of positive braids and generation properties for the Chow groups of flag Richardson, projected Richardson, and brick varieties: namely, that these groups are generated integrally by the fundamental classes of their closed Richardson, positroid, and braid strata, respectively.

papers.title: Twisted Patterson-Sullivan densities on nilpotent covers for Anosov subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma<\mathsf{SL}(d,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free, Zariski-dense Borel-Anosov subgroup, and let $\varphi$ be a linear functional positive on the limit cone of $\Gamma$. For every $\chi \in \operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathbb R)$, we construct twisted $(\varphi,\chi)$-conformal densities and prove their existence, uniqueness and ergodicity. For every non-trivial normal subgroup $\Gamma_0\lhd\Gamma$ with nilpotent quotient, we classify the ergodic $\varphi$-conformal densities of $\Gamma_0$ in terms of characters of $\Gamma/\Gamma_0$. Up to scaling, they are naturally parametrized by $\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma/\Gamma_0,\mathbb R)$, and their dimensions are precisely the critical exponents of the corresponding twisted Poincar\'e series. We also prove a shadow lemma for twisted densities of normal subgroups, with estimates uniform over densities with fixed parameters, and a twisted Hopf-Tsuji-Sullivan theorem.

papers.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract:
We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma.
  This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.

papers.title: Logarithmic Stability for the Inverse Boundary Problem in Three-Dimensional Isotropic Elasticity
papers.abstract:
We establish logarithmic stability for the simultaneous recovery of both Lam\'e parameters in three-dimensional static isotropic elasticity from the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The $L^\infty(\Omega)$ estimate holds uniformly on every fixed bounded $C^{22}$ class of uniformly strongly convex coefficients, without prescribed exterior coefficients, agreement of boundary values or derivatives, or smallness assumptions on material gradients. For every integer $s\ge2$, we also obtain boundary stability estimates with exponents $(s-q)/s$ for all Cartesian derivatives of orders $0\le q<s$, where the measurement error $\delta$ is the operator-norm discrepancy between the Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps. These exponents are sharp on admissible classes containing a constant material satisfying the a priori inequalities strictly. On such classes, no uniform modulus of continuity exists for boundary derivatives of order $s$.
  The proof combines an exact four-component reduction with finite-regularity complex geometrical optics constructions, while deriving complete matrix-valued integral identities from the Betti identity for elastic displacements. An amplitude annihilated by the leading physical adjoint lift produces, at the first nonvanishing order, the third polarization in a rank-three characteristic quotient. Holomorphically weighted matrix moments, Cauchy--Plemelj factorization, and a fixed holomorphic projection then yield quantitative control of the relative transport and recovery of both coefficients. Boundary stability estimates and paired extensions transfer the analysis from an auxiliary common-exterior setting to the original measurement domain. The exact-data argument also establishes global uniqueness for $C^{22}$ Lam\'e parameters.

papers.title: On Convergence to Equilibrium for the Boltzmann Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We study relaxation of correlated solutions of the hard-cutoff Boltzmann hierarchy toward factorized Maxwellian equilibrium. We prescribe the Maxwellian's mass, momentum, and energy in each full particle coordinate, conditional on the others. Centering removes these conserved modes, but collisions still couple each centered level to the next. To control this forcing uniformly in particle number, we combine adapted second-order Sobolev tensor norms with geometric activity weights and prove $\frac12\frac{d}{dt}E_z(H(t))^2 +(\lambda-\sqrt{2}C_\Gamma z)D_z(H(t))^2\le0,$ where $H$ is the rescaled centered hierarchy, $E_z,D_z$ measure its energy and dissipation, and the coercivity and collision constants $\lambda,C_\Gamma$ are independent of particle number. For small activity $z$, dissipation absorbs the coupling and gives contraction and uniqueness in the hierarchy energy. Time-dependent weights yield level-proportional exponential decay. For global solutions, densities and observable generating functions converge to equilibrium, and connected pair correlations decay at twice the one-particle rate. The estimates apply to existing energy solutions. General existence remains an assumption, while statistical mixtures, including continuous laws, of sufficiently regular one-particle solutions uniformly close to the reference Maxwellian, with common conserved moments, provide examples.

papers.title: Homogenization of degenerate parabolic Signorini problems with vanishing storage and oscillating surface fluxes
papers.authors: Hermann Douanla, Rodrigue Kenne Bogning, Erick Tetsadjio
papers.abstract: We study the homogenization of a unilateral quasilinear parabolic problem in a periodically perforated medium. The model combines two degeneracies: the coefficient of the time derivative is non-negative and may vanish, while the directional diffusion weights are positive almost everywhere but need not be bounded away from zero. The exterior boundary carries a Signorini condition, and the holes carry an unscaled zero-mean flux oscillating on the diffusive time scale. For any family of microscopic solutions we prove strong space--time $L^2$ compactness through a weighted detection inequality, which replaces the Aubin--Lions lemma when the storage vanishes, and we recover spatial $H^1$ regularity of the limit by a closed-range argument for the weighted two-scale gradients. The limit solves a coupled two-scale problem in Minty form, and microscopic existence holds under joint monotonicity. Under a strengthened condition, the limit decouples into a macroscopic Signorini inequality whose uniqueness follows from an exponential regularization, without time regularity of the limit, and the whole family converges. The surface datum enters both the effective flux and the exterior boundary condition.

papers.title: Axisymmetric Navier--Stokes with Swirl: Regularity and Blow-Up Constraints
papers.abstract: For smooth finite-energy axisymmetric Navier--Stokes solutions with swirl, we give a continuation criterion in terms of the signed cumulative work of the actual post-cut source-generated meridional current, with quartic viscous dissipation counted once. In the stated strong Sobolev class the criterion is necessary and sufficient and requires neither a global circulation bound nor spatial moments. We also prove cumulative inward-compression criteria, collect quantitative necessary conditions at a first singular time, and give a complete-history mixed-residual test for noncontinuation. Auxiliary results quantify quartic dissipation, energy-funded source bounds, and causal source--receiver identities. An explicit smooth whole-space datum has positive newborn source production.

papers.title: $L^p$-regularity for fourth-order Schr\"odinger operators with unbounded or degenerate coefficients
papers.authors: Federica Gregorio, Chiara Spina, Cristian Tacelli
papers.abstract: We prove that operators of the form $A=-\Delta^{2}-V(x)$, with $|D V(x)|\leq \gamma V(x)^\frac{5}{4}+ C_\gamma$ for some $\gamma$ small enough and $C_\gamma$ positive constant, generate analytic semigroups in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for $1\leq p<\infty$ and in $C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Moreover, we characterize the maximal domain of such operators.

papers.title: Nonradial Finite-Time Blow-up for the Mass-Critical Inhomogeneous Biharmonic NLS
papers.authors: Ngoc Uyen Cong Nguyen, Van Duong Dinh
papers.abstract: We consider the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous biharmonic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ i\partial_tu=\Delta^2u-|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{8-2b}{N}}u, \quad 0<b<\min\{4,N/2\}. \] We prove that every $H^2(\mathbb R^N)$ solution with negative energy blows up in finite time, both forward and backward. No radial symmetry or finite-variance assumption is required. In particular, this rules out the global grow-up scenario in the previously known negative-energy blow-up alternative and establishes finite-time blow-up in the genuinely nonradial setting. The proof relies on a new localized virial argument exploiting the spatial inhomogeneity to control the localization errors.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and orbital stability of the Gross--Pitaevskii branch in a coupled defocusing Schr\"odinger system
papers.authors: Micha{\l} Kowalczyk, Jaros{\l}aw Mederski, Isidora Miranda
papers.abstract: We consider a one-dimensional coupled defocusing Schr\"odinger system with a nonzero background in its first component and finite mass in its second component. We prove global well-posedness in the full energy space, together with conservation of energy, bright mass, and total untwisted momentum. For all nonnegative coupling coefficients, every subsonic Gross--Pitaevskii soliton with vanishing second component is orbitally stable against perturbations of both components, including the zero-speed black soliton. At nonzero speed the proof uses a fixed energy--momentum functional augmented by the conserved bright mass. At zero speed it uses weighted coercivity and a local real lift of the momentum. We also identify the sharp threshold for positivity of the unaugmented bright energy and explain why this threshold is not a necessary condition for orbital stability.

papers.title: On the annular overdetermined problems with linear and power nonlinearities in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.authors: Jun Wang, Fei Xu, Yong Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study two classes of partially overdetermined elliptic problems on planar annular domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with a fixed inner circle and a free outer boundary. The Dirichlet values are prescribed to be $1$ and $0$ on the inner and outer boundaries, respectively, while the squared normal derivative is constant on the outer boundary. For the linear law $\Delta u=-\mu u$, we establish local bifurcation under a Dirichlet nonresonance condition. For the power law $\Delta u=u-u^p$ with $p>1$, we take the mean outer radius as the bifurcation parameter and construct large positive radial solutions on thin annuli. The limiting profile solves $-V''=V^p$ on an interval, and the principal mixed Dirichlet--Neumann eigenvalue of its linearization determines a constant $\kappa_p>0$. For every fixed inner radius $\lambda>0$ and every sufficiently large integer $K$, we obtain a critical radius $R_K=\lambda+\lambda\kappa_p/K+o(K^{-1})$ and a smooth local curve of positive solutions with noncircular, even, $2\pi/K$-periodic outer boundaries. The proof combines shape derivatives, spectral estimates, and the Crandall--Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem.

papers.title: A frequency localized maximum principle and its applications to time fractional equations with rough coefficients
papers.abstract: We establish a frequency localized maximum principle for parabolic second-order partial differential equations with the Caputo time fractional derivative $\partial_t^\alpha$ of order $\alpha\in(0,1)$. The leading coefficients are uniformly elliptic, measurable in time, and independent of space. We construct suitable equivalent norms on frequency localized subspaces of $L_\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$, for which a frequency localized maximum principle holds. The corresponding result may fail in the usual $L_\infty$ norm even for the classical heat equation. As an application, we prove existence, uniqueness, and regularity estimates in Sobolev-Zygmund spaces with Muckenhoupt weights in time for equations with spatially variable coefficients and zero initial data. The coefficients are strongly measurable in time with values in a H\"older-Zygmund space of positive order and uniformly bounded in this space.

papers.title: The Neumann problem for stochastic partial differential equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Neumann problem for second-order stochastic partial differential equations in the half space. The coefficients are random and merely measurable in time. We develop a class of weighted function spaces for this problem, and establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity results. In contrast to the Dirichlet problem, the Neumann problem admits solutions with improved boundary regularity under suitable assumptions on the coefficients and data.

papers.title: Curvature Effects on Boundary Accumulation of Self-Propelled Particles: A Fokker-Planck Approach
papers.authors: Jingyi Fu, Jinqi Liu, Benoit Perthame, Min Tang
papers.abstract: It is well known that self-propelled particles tend to accumulate near boundaries. Although the influence of boundary geometry on this accumulation has been extensively studied using individual-based models, a population-level PDE description becomes desirable when a large number of particles are involved. In this work, we investigate boundary accumulation of self-propelled particles confined in two-dimensional circular and annular domains. We develop Fokker--Planck models that qualitatively reproduce the behavior observed in individual-based simulations. The main contribution is the formulation of appropriate evolution equations for particles accumulated at the boundary, incorporating transitions between the interior free-swimming state and the boundary-contact state. Starting from a general spatial two-dimensional model, we simplify the associated boundary conditions by assuming radial symmetry and then design an exponentially weighted difference scheme that preserves the total mass of the coupled system. Because transitions between different particle states induce singular behavior near the boundary, establishing discrete mass conservation is nontrivial. In particular, the velocity space must be divided into two subdomains, with the resulting discontinuity treated explicitly. Stochastic simulations and numerical experiments are performed both to validate the proposed models and to investigate the effects of geometric and dynamical parameters on boundary accumulation.

papers.title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
papers.abstract:
We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-\lambda u \quad \text{in }\Omega. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory.
  For $\lambda>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $\lambda$ and constant for sufficiently small $\lambda$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $\lambda\to+\infty$.
  In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(\Omega)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]

papers.title: The fractional Calder\'on problem on finite Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: We study a Calder\'on-type inverse problem for the spectral fractional Laplacian on finite Cayley graphs. For a known self-adjoint operator, recovery from a single measurement reduces to two requirements: full rank of the boundary (exterior)-to-interior coupling and nonvanishing of the interior solution. We verify both requirements on Cartesian products of arbitrary finite groups with even cycles, using consecutive cyclic halves as the accessible and inaccessible sets. Fractionalization increases the coupling rank, and one fixed nonnegative nonzero input determines every nonnegative potential. Our argument relies on a discrete maximum principle and an explicit resolvent formula.

papers.title: Sharp Wasserstein stability and small-delay thresholds for evolution equations with measure-valued principal-part delays
papers.abstract: We study the dependence of solutions to coercive evolution equations on the law of a measure-valued delay acting through the principal spatial operator. For non-negative delay measures of equal mass, transport couplings and the time-translation modulus of one reference trajectory yield quantitative kernel-stability estimates. Fractional temporal regularity gives a Wasserstein rate, with explicit glueing and data criteria for its application. For moving point delays in a diffusion model, a solution-level lower bound matches both the rate and its dependence on the kernel mass. This matching estimate holds for zero prescribed history and uniformly bounded forcing in the natural dual energy space. The results also quantify concentration to positive delays and approximation by atomic quadrature. Separately, we determine a sharp class-level threshold for energy bounds uniform in the delay location. At the critical threshold, any fixed scalar mode is spectrally stable, but uniform space--time energy control fails in a small-delay, high-frequency limit. Above the threshold, the growth has an explicit asymptotic logarithmic rate.

papers.title: Symmetry and Monotonicity for Subcritical Fractional Hartree Equations with Singular Sets of Zero Capacity
papers.authors: Guangze Gu, Aleks Jevnikar, Zhipeng Yang
papers.abstract: We study positive weak singular solutions of the subcritical fractional Hartree equation \[ (-\Delta)^s u = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma} \frac{u^p(y)}{|x-y|^\mu}d y \right)u^q \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma, \] where \(0<s<1\), \(N>2s\), \(0<\mu<N\), and \(\Gamma\subset\{x_1=0\}\) is compact with zero \((s,2)\)-capacity. For solutions with a nonremovable singular point on $\Gamma$, we prove hyperplane symmetry and strict transverse monotonicity under global Lebesgue integrability conditions. For $N\ge2$, we also prove these conclusions under upper bounds on $p$ and $q$, using only the integrability required for weak solutions. We also establish local regularity and construct solutions with logarithmic singularities along a line segment.

papers.title: Universal H\"older estimates for stable solutions to semilinear equations of fractional order
papers.abstract: We establish universal interior H\"older and fractional energy estimates for stable solutions of $(-\Delta)^su=f(u)$, $0<s<1$, with $f\in C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R})$ nonnegative and convex. The bounds depend only on a weighted $L^1$ norm of the solution and hold under optimal conditions on the dimension and the fractional order.
