Third, we characterize the obstruction to removing regularization at fixed particle number and establish a separate conditional density-level convergence criterion under uniform regularity and approximation assumptions, using relative entropy. A heat-equation counterexample shows that an unregularized density-level Picard iteration can diverge. Atomic Coulomb and simultaneous particle-zero-regularization limits remain open.

papers.title: The $(n-2)$-linear restriction estimate in $\mathbb R^n$
papers.abstract: We present a proof for the $(n-2)$-linear extension estimate for curved surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge5$, at the local product exponent $2(n-1)/(n-2)^2$, with an arbitrarily small power loss. The hypotheses are transversality of the normals and nondegeneracy of the compressed shape operators on their common two-dimensional orthogonal complement. The argument combines polynomial partitioning, a descent through algebraic varieties, localized multilinear restriction, and positive packet-energy estimates.

papers.title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
papers.authors: Max Fathi, Arnaud Guillin, Cyril Labb\'e, Justin Salez
papers.abstract: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].

papers.title: Two-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equations with critical long-range correlations
papers.abstract: We study a $(2+1)$-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equation in which the noise is correlated like $f(\log |z|)/|z|^2$ as $|z|\to \infty$. Under an appropriate rescaling and logarithmic attenuation, we show that the limiting two-point statistics are given by the solution to a forward-backward stochastic differential equation. As shown in the work of Cosco, Cottini, and Donadini (2025), with whose results our study agrees in the linear case, the interesting feature of the two-dimensional, long-range problem is that one sees a varying influence on the limiting distribution from a range of spatial scales. We show that this phenomenon appears in the decoupling function for the limiting object and that the function $f$ modulates the weight of the contribution of each spatial scale.

papers.title: Young Parabolic PDEs and the Martingale Problem for Young SDEs
papers.authors: Fabio Bugini, Michele Coghi, Khoa L\^e, Chengcheng Ling
papers.abstract: Under mild regularity assumptions, we prove that the martingale problem associated with the hybrid Young--Lyons--It\^o differential equation admits a unique solution in the natural class of solutions satisfying Krylov-type estimates, thereby establishing probabilistic weak well-posedness. Our proof relies on an analysis of the associated Kolmogorov equations, which are Young-type parabolic PDEs with irregular coefficients. The resulting theory for such Young-type parabolic PDEs is also of independent interest.

papers.title: Average lower bound on magnetic double-well tunneling with asymptotically large well separation
papers.authors: Charles L. Fefferman, Say-Yeon Kwon, Jacob Shapiro, Michael I. Weinstein
papers.abstract: We study tunneling between two identical, smooth, compactly supported potential wells in a constant perpendicular magnetic field, with the coupling and magnetic field fixed and the well separation tending to infinity. For a sufficiently small positive magnetic field, we prove lower bounds on the hopping coefficient and on the splitting of the two lowest eigenvalues outside a set of separations of density zero. If the well centers are separated by $2d_1$ and the magnetic field strength is $b\lambda$, the lower bounds have the form $e^{-b\lambda d_1^2-Cd_1^{1+\delta}}$ for every fixed $\delta\in(0,1)$. No radial or reflection symmetry of the single-well potential is assumed. The proof combines the explicit Landau resolvent kernel with a complex analytic estimate for logarithmic averages of the hopping coefficient.

papers.title: Weak solutions for weak turbulence models in electrostatic plasmas
papers.abstract: The weak turbulence model, also known as the quasilinear theory in plasma physics, has been a cornerstone in modeling resonant particle-wave interactions in plasmas. Stemming from the Vlasov-Poisson/Maxwell system under the weak turbulence assumption, incorporating the random phase approximation and ergodicity, it takes the form of a integro-differential system, which describes the time dynamics of particle distribution and wave spectrum. The interaction between particles and waves can be treated as a stochastic process, whose transition probability bridges the momentum space and the spectral space. To our knowledge, there is no preceding rigorous analytical work for the quasilinear theory addressed in this manuscript. In this paper, we establish the existence of global weak solutions to the one-dimensional electrostatic quasilinear model for nonnegative, smooth, rapidly decaying initial particle distributions and nonnegative, smooth wave spectra compactly supported in a positive wave-number band. The construction uses the resonance condition to reduce the coupled system to a scalar degenerate parabolic equation, together with uniform estimates and strong convergence of the gradients of regularized approximations. When the initial wave spectrum is positive throughout a single band, we further characterize the equilibrium selected by this approximation procedure. The equilibrium uniquely minimizes a quadratic functional over a nonnegative cone and admits a geometric construction through the least concave majorant of a primitive determined by the initial data. The limiting particle distribution is non-increasing on the corresponding resonant interval and forms plateaus wherever the equilibrium auxiliary function is positive. A relative-entropy argument establishes long-time convergence to this equilibrium.

papers.title: Singular semilinear elliptic equations in half-spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the monotonicity of positive solutions to the problem $-\Delta u = f(u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N_+ := \{(x',x_N)\in\mathbb{R}^N \mid x_N>0 \}$ under zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a possible singular nonlinearity $f$. In some situations, we can derive a precise estimate on the blow-up rate of $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\eta}$ as $x_N \to 0^+$, where $(\eta,e_N)>0$, and obtain a classification result. The main tools we use are the method of moving planes and the sliding method.

papers.title: A P\"oschl--Teller approximation to the wave equation outside a torus
papers.abstract: We prove dispersive estimates for an approximation to the wave equation in the exterior of a torus. Because no separation of variables into a basis of eigenfunctions and eigenvalues exists in toroidal coordinates for the time harmonic problem, we introduce a related approximate operator for the Dirichlet Laplacian in the exterior of a torus. The approximate operator separates into Schr\"odinger operators with P\"oschl-Teller potentials after freezing $N=N_0$ in the conjugated Laplacian. The operator here which we develop is related to the so-called Mehler-Fock kernel. Using the known solution to the eigenvector and eigenvalue problem of P\"oschl-Teller, a high-frequency analysis of the approximate operator for the wave equation can be made accurately. The operator for this problem gives an angularly truncated $L^1\rightarrow L^{\infty}$ dispersive estimate on compact coordinate collars. Duhamel's principle controls its error for the corresponding exterior wave operator with Dirichlet Laplacian.

papers.title: Boundary estimates for singular elliptic problems involving a gradient term
papers.abstract: We study bounded positive weak solutions of the singular quasilinear problem $-\Delta_p u+\vartheta|\nabla u|^q=u^{-\gamma}+f(u)$ in a bounded $C^2$ domain, with zero Dirichlet boundary data, where $p>1$, $\gamma>0$, $0<q\le p$, $\vartheta\ge0$, and $f$ is continuous up to zero and locally Lipschitz on $(0,\infty)$. We establish sharp boundary asymptotics for the solution and its directional derivatives. For $\gamma>1$ the leading profile is a universal power of the boundary distance; for $\gamma=1$ it is logarithmic, with the sharp constant $(p/(p-1))^{1/p}$. In both cases the normalized gradient converges uniformly to the inward normal multiplied by the corresponding constant. For $0<\gamma<1$ we prove global $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity and a classical Hopf boundary estimate. We also obtain the optimal Sobolev integrability threshold and the sharp logarithmic modulus of continuity. Finally, positivity of the total source on the solution range yields symmetry and monotonicity in symmetric domains strictly convex in one direction; when $N\ge2$ and $\vartheta>0$, we assume $q\ge\max\{1,p/2\}$.

papers.title: Well-Posedness of Fully Nonlinear PDEs on Star-Shaped Networks with Nonlinear Kirchhoff Conditions
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish the well-posedness of fully nonlinear partial differential equations on star-shaped networks subject to nonlinear Kirchhoff conditions at the junction. The branchwise operators may be discontinuous across the junction, and uniform ellipticity is required only in a neighborhood of the vertex. Our approach relies on the construction of auxiliary test functions solving suitable nonlinear ordinary differential equations, whose structure allows us to control the viscosity inequalities at the junction. We first show that generalized Kirchhoff viscosity solutions in the sense of Lions-Souganidis satisfy the strong Kirchhoff condition. Combining these auxiliary functions with an affine perturbation of supersolutions and precise junction gradient estimates, we establish a comparison principle for bounded semicontinuous viscosity sub- and supersolutions. Existence and uniqueness are then addressed through Perron's method and the comparison principle. Finally, we discuss first-order junction problems and a possible transmission condition arising from vanishing viscosity.

papers.title: Energy minimizers in a periodic phase transition model of light-matter interaction in nematic liquid crystals
papers.authors: Panayotis Smyrnelis, Marcel G. Clerc, Manuel Diaz-Zuniga, Micha{\l} Kowalczyk
papers.abstract: In this paper we complete the study of global minimizers of a forced, non autonomous, one dimensional, phase transition model, initiated in [8]. Motivated by the recent findings in [9], revealing new configurations of topological structures in light, we consider a forcing term having two periods. We show that depending on the strength of the forcing, at most two thresholds that determine the structure of the minimizers (kinks) are attained. These kinks are now a combination of three types observed experimentally, and they may have at most three zeros. The existence of these complex types of phase transition follows from a periodic one dimensional model of matter-light interaction in nematic liquid crystal based on a thin sample limit of the Oseen-Frank energy. We show that the qualitative behaviour of global minimizers is consistent with the original model.

papers.title: Multiplicity of bound states for a class of nonlinear Dirac equations on generalized star graphs with potentials
papers.authors: Guangze Gu, Ziwei Li, Michael Ruzhansky, Zhipeng Yang
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate the existence and multiplicity of bound states for a class of nonlinear Dirac equations on a generalized star graph \(\mathcal{G}\): \[ -ic\,\sigma_1\,\partial_xu+mc^2\sigma_3u+V(x)u=f(|u|)u,\qquad x\in\mathcal{G}, \] where \(V:\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, \(f\in C^1([0,\infty))\), \(m>0\), \(c>0\), and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_3\) are the Pauli matrices. Under suitable monotonicity and growth assumptions on \(f\), a uniform spectral gap and sufficiently long constant-potential intervals on \(k\) terminal edges yield at least \(2^k-1\) bound states, distinct up to a constant phase. The constant potentials on these intervals may differ. The construction uses half-line solutions and a uniform inverse estimate. For potentials tending to a constant at infinity, we prove compactness below the full-line ground level. In the flat-well setting, the solutions localized near individual terminal vertices lie below this level and provide a ground state through the generalized Nehari minimization. In particular, one localized solution is obtained for each minimum component containing a long terminal interval.

papers.title: Fully localised three-dimensional solitary water waves on Beltrami flows with strong surface tension
papers.abstract: Fully localised three-dimensional solitary waves are steady water waves which are evanescent in every horizontal direction. This paper presents an existence theory for such waves under the assumptions that the relative vorticity and velocity fields are parallel (`Beltrami flows'), that the free surface of the water takes the form $\{z=\eta(x,y)\}$ for some function $\eta: {\mathbb R}^2\rightarrow{\mathbb R}$, and that the influence of surface tension is sufficiently strong. The governing equations are formulated as a single equation for $\eta$, which is then reduced to a perturbation of the KP-I equation. This equation has recently been shown to have a family of nondegenerate localised solutions, and an application of a suitable variant of the implicit-function theorem shows that they persist under perturbations.

papers.title: Feedback Stabilization and Tracking for Heat Equations Using Thermo-Plasmonic Nanoparticles as Actuators
papers.authors: Arpan Mukherjee, S\'ergio S. Rodrigues, Mourad Sini
papers.abstract: We propose a feedback strategy to track prescribed heat profiles using plasmonic nanoparticles as actuators. Starting from a thermo--plasmonic Maxwell--heat model, we use a time-domain discrete effective description in which the generated heat is approximated by a superposition of heat kernels centered at particle locations with amplitudes governed by a coupled Volterra system. We recast this dynamics as a heat equation on a bounded domain with finitely many point actuators and design a tracking feedback based on pointwise evaluations of $\mathcal A^{-1}y$, where $\mathcal A=I-A_0$ and $A_0$ is the Neumann diffusion operator. Working in the natural $V'$ setting with $V=D(\mathcal A)$, we prove exponential stabilization of the tracking error via distribution-actuator theory. For non-equilibrium reference profiles, we add a constant feedforward term and a low-mode fixed-point pre-compensation on $X_N$, ensuring exact steady matching on $X_N$ and an explicit bound on the residual tail mismatch.

papers.title: Schr\"odinger ultrahyperbolic equations with singular coefficients
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate the Cauchy problem for Schr\"odinger ultrahyperbolic equations with singular (less than continuous) coefficients. We prove $H^\infty$ well-posedness in the very weak sense under suitable assumptions of the distributional structure of the coefficients and decay on the lower order terms. Consistency is proven with the classical $H^\infty$-results when the equation coefficients are smooth.

papers.title: Sublinear elliptic equations with a sharp change of sign in the nonlinearity
papers.authors: M\'onica Clapp, Alberto Salda\~na, Delia Schiera
papers.abstract: We study the semilinear indefinite elliptic problem \[ -\Delta u = Q_\Omega |u|^{p-2}u \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N, \] where $Q_\Omega = \chi_\Omega - \chi_{\mathbb{R}^N \setminus \Omega}$, $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded smooth subset, $N \geq 3$, and $1 \leq p < 2$, with $p=1$ corresponding to the sign nonlinearity. Using a variational approach, we investigate the uniqueness or multiplicity of nonnegative solutions depending on the shape of $\Omega$ and the existence of different types of nodal solutions. We also show that all solutions have compact support and analyze how the support of the ground state depends on $p$, proving convergence to the whole space as $p\to 2^{-}$ and identifying some qualitative features such as starshapedness and Lipschitz regularity of the support. We also establish a link between these problems and a two-phase Serrin-type torsion overdetermined problem.

papers.title: Optimal $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary for fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy
papers.authors: Junior da Silva Bessa, Jehan Oh
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish optimal $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary for viscosity solutions of fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy law and oblique boundary conditions. The approach developed here relies on first deriving uniform boundary H\"older estimates for perturbed models with oblique boundary data in ``almost $C^{1}$-flat'' domains. Building upon these estimates, the desired regularity is obtained through a compactness and stability framework for viscosity solutions. As a byproduct of our analysis, we determine the optimal H\"older exponent for solutions when the governing operator is quasiconvex or quasiconcave. In addition, we establish an improved regularity result along vanishing points of the source term.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of Landau solutions to the MHD system and energy decay
papers.authors: Nicola De Nitti, Yun Wang, Shaoheng Zhang
papers.abstract: We consider the three-dimensional incompressible MHD system. Any weak solution satisfying a strong energy inequality is $L^2$-asymptotically stable around a Landau solution. Under an additional integrability assumption on the initial perturbation, we also obtain an explicit algebraic decay rate for the $L^2$-norm of the velocity and magnetic perturbations.

papers.title: Magnetic uncertainty in variable geometry
papers.authors: Luca Fanelli, Yilin Song, Ying Wang, Jiqiang Zheng, Ruihan Zhou
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study Hardy-type uncertainty principles and unique continuation properties for linear covariant Schrodinger equations with variable coefficients in the presence of bounded electric and magnetic potentials. Under suitable smallness assumptions on the leading coefficients, we prove that any solution exhibiting super-quadratic exponential decay at two distinct times must vanish identically. Under an additional structural assumption on the coefficient matrix $G$, we further establish a Hardy-type result at the quadratic exponential scale. We also obtain an analogous uniqueness result for the heat equation with variable-coefficient magnetic perturbations.
  Our results unify and extend previous works in two directions: they recover the constant-coefficient covariant case treated by Barcelo-Fanelli-Gutierrez-Ruiz-Vilela when $G=I$, and the variable-coefficient non-magnetic case considered by Federico-Li-Yu when $A=0$. The proofs combine logarithmic convexity arguments with Carleman estimates adapted to variable-coefficient covariant Schr\"odinger and parabolic flows. Although our approach follows the general strategy introduced by Escauriaza-Kenig-Ponce-Vega, substantial new difficulties arise from the interaction between the variable metric and the magnetic structure, which requires new weight functions and refined commutator estimates.

papers.title: Solutions to Monge-Amp\`ere Equations with Low Codimensional singularities
papers.abstract: We construct solutions to Monge-Amp\`ere equations whose Monge-Amp\`ere measures contain singular components supported on low codimensional sets. We also study the regularity of such solutions. To motivate our construction, we present examples arising from optimal transport where the potential of optimal transport maps satisfy Monge-Amp\`ere equations similar to the ones we study.

papers.title: Stability of optimal transport maps and second variation of the 2-Monge-Kantorovich distance
papers.authors: F. -U. Caja-Lopez, Matias G. Delgadino, Jun Kitagawa
papers.abstract: We establish several quantitative stability estimates for optimal transport maps between non-degenerate densities on uniformly convex domains for the quadratic cost. Under H\"older regularity assumptions, we prove Lipschitz $L^{2}$ (respectively $C^{0,\alpha}$) stability estimates for optimal transport maps in terms of the $2$-Monge--Kantorovich distance (respectively $L^{p}$ distances) between pairs of source and target densities. When the continuity assumption is removed, we obtain a Lipschitz $L^{2}$ stability estimate for the Brenier potentials in terms of the $L^{2}$ distance between the source and target densities. The proofs rely on a precise characterization of the linear response of the Brenier potential along smooth interpolations of the data, obtained by linearizing the Monge--Amp\`ere equation in divergence form. As a further application of this approach, we derive an explicit formula for the second variation of the quadratic Monge--Kantorovich distance.

papers.title: Resonant Microstructures as Dirac-type Sources for Acoustic Wave Control
papers.abstract: We study finite-time acoustic wave tracking using effective interior Dirac-type actuators generated by clusters of subwavelength resonant bubbles driven from exterior transducers. Starting from a time-domain point-interaction approximation, the full scattering problem is reduced to a finite-dimensional delayed system of interacting retarded monopoles. After localization to a bounded observation domain, we formulate the tracking problem on a prescribed finite-dimensional Dirichlet spectral subspace. At the ideal level, a full-rank spatial coupling condition yields exact tracking of arbitrary sufficiently smooth compatible trajectories in this subspace by interior point sources. These ideal actuators are realized using small, high-contrast bubbles, whose Laplace-domain transfer operator encodes the Minnaert resonances and collective attenuation. The principal mode of each cluster is isolated by the Perron--Frobenius structure and the intra-cluster spectral gap. Clusters tuned to the same band are then treated as a collective resonant block. The selected Dirichlet bands are matched with the corresponding Minnaert bands. For prescribed slowly time-modulated resonant pressure profiles, with sufficiently flat initialization, we construct causal exterior controls and obtain a quantitative tracking estimate on every fixed time interval $[0,T]$. In contrast, on frequency ranges uniformly separated from the Minnaert resonances, the actuator gain is $O(\varepsilon)$ and the corresponding realization cost is asymptotically unbounded as $\varepsilon \ll 1$, $\varepsilon$ being the maximum radius of the bubbles. Thus the Minnaert resonances convert accessible exterior excitations into robust effective interior controls.

papers.title: The quantitative isoperimetric inequality: A calibration argument
papers.abstract: We give a short proof of the quantitative isoperimetric inequality. Our argument is based on a notion of quantitative calibrations which induce a natural distance controlling both the Fraenkel asymmetry and the tilt excess. The proof of our key result which can be viewed as a nonlinear, geometric version of Fuglede's result in $BV$ is direct and self-contained. In particular, we do not make any use of regularity theory for almost minimizers.

papers.title: An inverse free boundary problem
papers.authors: C\u{a}t\u{a}lin I. C\^{a}rstea, Matti Lassas, Jinpeng Lu, Lauri Oksanen, Ziyao Zhao
papers.abstract: We study inverse problems for the elliptic and parabolic obstacle problems from boundary measurements. For the classical elliptic obstacle problem with strictly superharmonic obstacle function, we show that the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map admits a one-sided linearization at every boundary datum lying strictly above the obstacle. The linearized map is the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a rough Dirichlet problem on the a priori unknown non-contact set. We show that these linearized Cauchy data uniquely determine the non-contact set up to set of Sobolev $2$-capacity zero and consequently determine the obstacle. Our result applies to the inverse problem for a parabolic obstacle problem where both the coefficient and the obstacle function are time-independent by reducing to the elliptic inverse problem.

papers.title: The scattering matrix for the p-form Laplacian on asymptotically conic manifolds
papers.abstract: The Hodge decomposition at infinity gives rise to distinct tangential scattering channels for differential forms on asymptotically conic manifolds. We construct co-closed generalized eigenforms for the Hodge Laplacian on $p$-forms in dimension $n\geq 3$ and analyze the resulting Bessel and Hankel systems. From these we determine the scattering matrix modulo smoothing operators, identifying it as a Fourier integral operator associated to the time $\pi$ geodesic flow and whose principal symbol encodes fibre-wise parallel transport with respect to the Levi-Civita connection on differential forms. In this setting this lifts the main result of Melrose and Zworski in [24] to differential forms and identifies additional scattering phase. The construction also yields a spectral representation in the co-closed sector, including a Stone-type formula and a functional calculus. In dimension $3$ and degree $p=1$, this framework describes divergence-free fields and thus the electric-field component of Maxwell's equations.

papers.title: Fastest-Species Selection in Critical Multispecies Competition-Diffusion Systems via an Entropy Approach
papers.abstract: We study an $N$-species competition--diffusion system with a common competition term, for which the associated ODE system admits infinitely many equilibria. For $N=2$, Alfaro and Xiao \cite{AlfaroXiao2023} studied the long-time behavior of solutions with compactly supported initial data by constructing precise super- and sub-solutions. For $N \geq 3$, the absence of a comparison principle for the entire system presents a major difficulty. Using a weighted entropy method, we prove that every bounded nonnegative traveling profile connecting nonzero equilibria is constant, without imposing any monotonicity assumption. For nontrivial compactly supported initial populations, we further show that the species with the strictly largest Fisher-KPP speed excludes all slower species and spreads at its scalar Fisher-KPP speed. Finally, we establish heat-type lower bounds for the slower species, revealing a bump phenomenon despite their uniform extinction.

papers.title: A counterexample to Kenig's conjecture for the Laplace double-layer operator
papers.abstract: We disprove Kenig's 1994 spectral-radius conjecture for the double-layer operator in every dimension $d\ge2$. For every $t>1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, we construct a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with connected boundary such that the double-layer operator on $L^2$ with respect to the surface measure has $\pm \mathrm{i} t$ in its Fredholm essential spectrum. In particular, the essential spectral radius is greater than $1/2$. In the plane, the boundary may be chosen differentiable everywhere and smooth away from a single point. Our planar construction develops a refinement mechanism that produces unbounded growth of adjoint resolvent solutions with fixed forcing while keeping the graph slopes uniformly bounded. A closed recursion for the density and its image under an auxiliary singular integral reduces the growth estimate to a certified inequality for Hermitian $2\times2$ matrices. The certificate uses continuous estimates, exact rational arithmetic and rigorous interval enclosures. Localisation and rescaled graph insertions then produce a weakly null sequence of normalised approximate eigenvectors for the adjoint double-layer operator on one bounded boundary. A compact intertwining relation on Cartesian products of the planar domain with cubes gives the higher-dimensional examples without changing the spectral parameter.

papers.title: Dimension-dependent symmetry breaking in a diffusive nonlocal interaction model
papers.authors: Dohyun Kim, Hansol Park, Woojoo Shim
papers.abstract: We study the equilibrium structure and long-time behavior of a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with diffusion and nonlocal interactions generated by squared simplex volumes. For $1\leq n<d$, the stationary states are isotropic Gaussian measures, and every solution converges to the equilibrium determined by its conserved mean. At $n=d$, the free energy fixes only the covariance determinant, allowing a continuum of anisotropic Gaussian equilibria when $d\geq2$. We establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial probability measures with finite second moment, identify stationary states with the global minimizers of the free energy, and prove convergence in quadratic Wasserstein distance with explicit exponential rates.

papers.title: Multidimensional fractional material derivative: measure-valued solutions and probabilistic properties
papers.abstract: We analyze a nonlocal operator in space and time, called the multidimensional fractional material derivative. We derive its pointwise representation, which allows us to study its other properties. We define an inverse operator, called fractional material integral, and derive its pointwise representation. Furthermore, we analyze a class of linear partial differential equations, which corresponds to deterministic descriptions of the scaling limits of multidimensional L\'evy walks, in which transport is driven by a multidimensional fractional material derivative with a speed vector integrated with respect to a suitable probability measure and a distributional source term. Using Fourier-Laplace transform techniques and a direct convolution-kernel construction, we prove the existence and uniqueness of exponentially integrable measure solutions for measure data. Moreover, we identify a necessary and sufficient condition on the source term for conservation of unit mass and provide separate sufficient conditions for non-negativity and weak convergence to $\delta_0$. We also prove weak continuity and self-similarity of the kernel and continuous dependence on the directional distribution.

papers.title: Existence and non-existence of extremal functions for inequalities of Bliss-Moser type
papers.authors: Yanyan Guo, Huxiao Luo, Bernhard Ruf
papers.abstract: We establish a concentration--compactness theory for a one-dimensional singular Moser-type functional with logarithmic weight function $$\sup\limits_{v\in E }\int_0^1 e^{\left(\log\frac{e}{s}+\gamma\log\log\frac{e}{s}\right)\frac{v^2(s)}{s}}ds<\infty,~\gamma\in[0,1],$$ where $$E:= \left\{u \in H^{1}(0, 1): u(0) = 0, \int_0^1 |u'|^2dx=1\right\}.$$ In particular, we prove compactness for all normalized sequences in the subcritical range $\gamma<1$, thereby resolving an open problem proposed in [J. M. do \'{O}, B. Ruf and P. Ubilla, CVPDE 2023]. We also study the critical Bliss-Moser inequality: \begin{equation}\nonumber \sup\limits_{v\in E }I^c(v)< +\infty,\quad I^c(v)=\int_0^1 e^{\left(\log\frac{e}{s}+\log\log\frac{e}{s}+cs\right)\frac{v^2(s)}{s}}ds. \end{equation} For any $c\in(-\infty,+\infty)$, we determine the sharp concentration level $$\sup_{v_j\in E,v_j~\text{is~NCS}}\limsup\limits_{j\to\infty} I^c(v_j)=1+e^2,$$ and obtain explicit sufficient conditions for attainability under $c>c^*$ and non-attainability under $c<-c_*$. This results describe how linear perturbations govern the transition between compactness, concentration, and attainability at the critical level.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional defocusing cubic Schr\"odinger equation in $H^s$, $s>\frac{1}{2}$
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with arbitrary initial data in $H^s(\R^3)$, $s>\frac{1}{2}$, without radial symmetry. The proof combines the $I$-method with long-time $L^2_{t,x}$ bounds for products of frequency-localized components of the nonlinear solution. The key high--low estimate follows from a directional interaction identity pairing high-frequency mass with low-frequency energy, together with an induction on frequency.

papers.title: Blow-up for a semilinear Tricomi equation in the oscillatory regime at the critical Strauss-type exponent
papers.authors: Diego Marcon, Wanderley Nunes do Nascimento, Matheus C. Santos
papers.abstract: We study finite-time blow-up for a semilinear shifted Tricomi equation with decreasing propagation speed and an oscillatory scale-invariant mass. We focus on the Strauss-type critical regime and prove that every weak solution with finite speed of propagation, arising from nonnegative nontrivial energy data satisfying a suitable localization condition, blows up in finite time. For sufficiently small initial data, we also obtain the corresponding critical exponential upper bound for the lifespan. The proof relies on a positive self-similar solution of the homogeneous adjoint equation represented by the Gauss hypergeometric function. Combined with a previously established lower bound for the nonlinear term and new estimates adapted to the critical case, this construction reduces the PDE problem to a nonlinear differential inequality. An ODE comparison argument then yields both finite-time blow-up and the lifespan estimate.

papers.title: Global well-posedness of defocusing cubic NLS in $M^{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness of the one-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in the modulation space $M^{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R})$. This space imposes no spatial decay and contains $C_b^2(\mathbb{R})$ as well as all absolutely convergent sums of plane waves. The result applies to arbitrary data in this space, including large smooth quasiperiodic profiles and their localized perturbations. The proof constructs a nonnegative density satisfying a local conservation law from forward Weyl ratios, which are defined through half-line square-integrable solutions of the associated spectral problem. A suitable nonlinear combination of localized integrals of this density controls the modulation norm. Finally, choosing the spatial localization scale and NLS scaling in a coordinated way makes the accumulated boundary flux small enough to continue every mild solution globally.

papers.title: On the Cauchy problem for the Tzitz\'{e}ica equation: Soliton resolution conjecture and asymptotic analysis
papers.abstract: We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitz\'eica equation, which is an important integrable model arising in affine differential geometry and characterizing proper affine spheres. Recently, Huang, Wang and Zhu (Math. Ann. \textbf{395}, 18 (2026)) reported the long-time asymptotic result for the Tzitz\'eica equation with purely continuous spectrum. Inspired by their work, we carry out a full asymptotic analysis of the Tzitz\'eica equation. Compared with the previous work, by developing the $\bar{\partial}$-nonlinear steepest descent method, we reveal that the solutions of the Tzitz\'eica equation exhibits three different asymptotic regions depending on $\xi:=x/t$. For the region $\xi\in(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$, where there are no stationary phase points, we rigorously prove that the solution satisfies $u(x,t)=O_\xi(t^{-1})$ for $\xi\ge1$ and $u(x,t)=2\pi i+O_\xi(t^{-1})$ for $\xi\le-1$. In the region $\xi\in(-1,1)$, the phase function $\theta(z)$ has two stationary phase points. The corresponding asymptotic approximations can be characterized with an $N$-soliton solution as well as an interaction term between soliton solutions and the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_K})$ with $0\le b_K<1/4$. In the transition regions $\{(x,t):1-\varepsilon<|\xi|<1\}$, the corresponding asymptotic approximation can be characterized by the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_\varepsilon})$ where $0\le b_\varepsilon<1/4$. Our results provide a rigorous analysis of the long-time asymptotic behavior of solutions of the Tzitz\'eica equation in different regions and confirm the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitz\'eica equation.

papers.title: Stability of 3D Stratified Plane Couette Flow: A New Lift-up Mechanism and Potential Vorticity
papers.abstract: Since the pioneering work of Taylor and Goldstein in 1931 laid the foundation for the study of parallel stratified shear flows, non-parallel configurations have received comparatively little attention. We study the stability of the 3D Boussinesq system near the plane Couette flow $V^*=(y,0,0)$ under the vertically stratified background $\eta^*=\alpha z$. The shear and stratification directions are perpendicular. This geometry produces two structural effects that are absent in the parallel configuration: an additional nonlocal coupling in the non-zero-mode system, which obstructs a directly useful symmetrization, and a wave-shear coupled lift-up mechanism for the zero modes. The $L^p$ transient growth due to the lift-up effect can be suppressed either by sufficiently strong stratification (for $p>2$) or under suitable assumptions on the initial data (for $p\geq 2$). To study the nonzero-mode system, we introduce a reformulation based on the linearized potential vorticity (PV), a fundamental quantity in geophysical fluid dynamics, to recover a better energy structure. We establish the inviscid damping of $u_{1,\neq}$ and $u_{2,\neq}$. We further apply the linearized PV formulation to study the linear stability of the tilted Couette flow. Finally, we use this formulation to prove the nonlinear stability for perturbations on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$.

papers.title: Global H\"older estimates for linearized Monge-Amp\`ere equations in divergence form with applications to dual semigeostrophic equations and periodic homogenization
papers.authors: Guoqing Cui, Chong Gu, Nam Q. Le, Ling Wang, Bin Zhou
papers.abstract: We establish interior and global H\"older estimates for linearized Monge-Amp\`ere equations in divergence form in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, when the Hessian determinant of the convex Monge-Amp\`ere potential is bounded above and below by positive constants and the vector field on the right-hand side is bounded. The estimates use the $L^p$ norm of the solution for any $p>1$. A key ingredient is an $L^1$ estimate, with appropriate decay rates, for the gradient of the Green's function of the linearized Monge-Amp\`ere operator in small sections, uniform with respect to the pole. As applications, we obtain uniform H\"older estimates for the time derivatives of the primal and dual potentials in the three-dimensional periodic dual semigeostrophic system when the initial density is bounded away from zero and infinity, and establish a linear convergence rate for periodic homogenization of the Monge-Amp\`ere equation.

papers.title: Sharp Truncated Difference Estimates for Nonlocal Nonconvex Functionals Defined by Superlevel Sets
papers.authors: Feng Dai, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Yirui Zhao
papers.abstract: Let $N\in\mathbb N$ and $p\in[1,\infty)$. In this article, we consider a family $\{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ of nonlocal nonconvex functionals with a real parameter $\gamma$ and establish two truncated difference estimates bounded by these functionals with the sharp range of $\gamma$; that is, for any $\gamma\in(-\infty,-1]$, any $\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, any cube $Q\subset\mathbb R^N$, and any measurable function $g:Q\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\int_Q\int_Q\left[\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|-\lambda|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}{\ell(Q)^{1+\gamma/p}}\right]_+^p\,dx\,dy\\ &\quad\lesssim \lambda^p\mathop{\int_Q\int_Q}\limits_{\frac{|g(x)-g(y)|}{|x-y|^{1+\gamma/p}}>\lambda}\left[\frac{|x-y|}{\ell(Q)}\right]^{\gamma-N}\,dx\,dy=:\frac{\Phi_{\lambda,p}^{\gamma}(g;Q)}{\ell(Q)^{\gamma-N}}, \end{align*} where the implicit positive constant depends only on $N$, $p$, and $\gamma$. For $\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, the above estimate holds with the left-most integrand replaced by $\frac{\min\{|g(x)-g(y)|^p,\lambda^p|x-y|^{p+\gamma}\}}{\ell(Q)^{p+\gamma}}$. As applications, these estimates yield related nonlocal Poincar\'e inequalities with the sharp range of $\gamma$, and also recover the known $\Gamma$-liminf lower bounds and characterizations of Sobolev and BV spaces in terms of the liminf of the functionals $\{\Phi^\gamma_{\lambda,p}\}_{\lambda\in(0,\infty)}$ for all $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}\setminus(-1,0]$. We investigate further applications to compactness and variational problems as well as a new VMO criterion. Inspired by a recent work of R. L. Frank, we develop an elementary approach based on dyadic iteration of truncated differences along line segments, which allows us to treat the aforementioned problems in a unified way.

papers.title: Low Mach number limit of the full Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions and large temperature variations
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Gu, Song Jiang, Qiangchang Ju, Yaobin Ou
papers.abstract: In this paper, we rigorously justify the low Mach number limit of the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations in a three-dimensional smooth bounded domain, subject to the no-slip boundary condition for the velocity and well-prepared initial data. In the presence of heat conduction and large temperature variations, we establish the uniform estimates for strong solutions on a time interval independent of the Mach number by constructing an energy functional in a Sobolev framework. The no-slip boundary condition cannot provide the vorticity boundary relation used in the slip-boundary setting. To overcome this difficulty, a divergence-free Stokes lifting of the boundary trace for the time derivative of the modified velocity is employed to define a test function vanishing on the boundary, which enables the transfer of a priori estimates from the velocity to the temperature.

papers.title: Convexity preservation for first-order nonlinear evolution equations with Neumann-type boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We study preservation of spatial convexity for viscosity solutions of first order Hamilton-Jacobi evolution equations with Neumann-type boundary conditions in bounded convex domains. Under a monotonicity assumption on the Hamiltonian in the outward normal direction, every viscosity supersolution of the Neumann problem is also a state-constraint supersolution. This reduces the boundary difficulty to a state-constraint problem and enables us to prove convexity preservation via the convex-envelope argument established by Alvarez, Lasry and Lions (1997). We also obtain propagation estimates for semiconvexity and strong convexity under similar structural assumptions.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system
papers.abstract: We establish the existence and uniqueness, up to translation, of monotone viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system, provided the two end states satisfy the Rankine-Hugoniot and Lax entropy conditions and the shock strength is small. Taking the shock strength as a singular perturbation parameter, we reduce the profile equations by Fenichel's geometric singular perturbation theory to a scalar equation on a slow manifold and obtain the profile as a heteroclinic orbit. We also give pointwise estimates of the profiles and their derivatives up to fourth order, with explicit leading-order terms for the first derivatives.

papers.title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
papers.abstract:
Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics?
  The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.

papers.title: Global well-posedness of the periodic Majda-Biello systems in the resonant case
papers.abstract:
We study the Cauchy problem for the following Majda-Biello system in the resonant case $\alpha \in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$ on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}$. \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{rcl}
  u_{t} + u_{xxx} & = & - v v_x,
  v_{t} + \alpha v_{xxx} & = & - (uv)_{x},
  (u,v)|_{t=0} & = & (u_0,v_0), \end{array} \right. \quad x \in \mathbb{T}, \, t \in \mathbb{R}. \] Here, the initial data $u_0$ and $v_0$ live in the Sobolev space $H^{s}(\mathbb{T})$ and $u_0$ has zero mean over $\mathbb{T}$. We establish the optimal global well-posedness for the above system when $s\geq \min\{1, s_\alpha+\}$, where $s_\alpha$ is a constant depending only on $\alpha$, and $s_\alpha = \frac12$ for almost every $\alpha \in (0,4]\setminus\{1\}$. These indices match the sharp ones in the local theory obtained by Oh (Int. Math. Res. Not., 18:3516-3556, 2009). The main novelty of our proof is to introduce a third modified energy in the I-method by performing a partial correction to the second modified energy around the resonant region. This partial correction avoids the singularity in the full correction, and therefore makes it possible to pointwise bound the quintilinear multipliers arising in the time derivative of the third modified energy. Another feature in our proof is the combination of the Diophantine approximation theory with the sparsity of nearly resonant frequency pairs on the periodic lattice to obtain the key quadrilinear and quintilinear estimates, leading to an almost conservation law sufficient for the global iteration.

papers.title: Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing small elastic particles
papers.abstract:
This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $\gamma=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size.
  For $\gamma=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $\gamma\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\gamma=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $\gamma=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.

papers.title: Equivalence of local weak and Benjamini--Schramm formulations of Berry's random wave model
papers.abstract: Berry's random wave model predicts that high-energy eigenfunctions of classically chaotic systems can be modeled locally, at the wavelength scale, by the Gaussian monochromatic random wave. Several rigorous formulations of this prediction have been proposed. We prove the equivalence of two such formulations on a closed manifold: local weak limits and Benjamini--Schramm convergence of manifolds decorated by eigenfunctions. The latter considers pointed manifolds equipped with a smooth function, up to isometry, without recording local orthonormal coordinates. The key step is to recover the unaveraged local function law from its orthogonal average using translation invariance and the ergodicity of the random wave. Finally, either formulation implies strong inverse localization, allowing high-energy eigenfunctions to approximate arbitrary solutions of the Euclidean Helmholtz equation, with applications to their nodal sets.

papers.title: The Restricted Three-Body Problem as a Perturbed Duffing Equation
papers.abstract:
This paper investigates the restricted circular planar three-body problem. We prove that for every negative Jacobi constant of sufficiently large magnitude, the surface of unperturbed parabolic solutions breaks to induce homoclinic tangles for all but at most finitely many mass ratios of primaries.
  Our approach relies on reformulating the restricted three-body problem as a perturbed Duffing equation by introducing new coordinate transformations. This enables us to capture the order of the singularities involved through a renormalized Duffing Hamiltonian structure, to derive the existence and analytic dependence of the invariant manifolds on the mass ratio of the primaries, and to evaluate the Poincar\'e-Melnikov integral directly through the explicit homoclinic solution of the unperturbed Duffing equation.
  Compared to existing works, our proof is significantly simpler and more direct. Moreover, the paper is self-contained: we do not rely on McGehee's analysis in \cite{Mc} to justify the applicability of the Poincar\'e-Melnikov method.

papers.title: Quantitative convergence for displacement monotone Mean Field Games of control
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish quantitative convergence results for both open and closed-loop Nash equilibria of N-player stochastic differential games in the setting of Mean Field Games of Controls (MFGC), a class of models where interactions among agents occur through both states and controls. Our analysis covers a general class of non-separable Hamiltonians satisfying a displacement monotonicity condition, along with mild regularity and growth conditions at infinity. A major novelty of our work is the rigorous treatment of a nontrivial fixed-point problem on a space of measures, which arises naturally in the MFGC formulation. Unlike prior works that either restrict to separable Hamiltonians - rendering the fixed-point map trivial - or assume convergence or regularity properties of the fixed point map, we develop a detailed structural analysis of this equation and its N-player analogue. This leads to new regularity results for the fixed-point maps and, in turn, to quantitative convergence of open-loop equilibria. We further derive sharp a priori estimates for the N-player Nash system, enabling us to control the discrepancy between open and closed-loop strategies, and thus to conclude the convergence of closed-loop equilibria. Our framework also accommodates common noise in a natural way.

papers.title: Spectrum of the wave equation with Dirac damping on a compact star graph
papers.abstract: We consider the wave equation with a distributional Dirac damping and Dirichlet boundary conditions on a compact interval. It is shown that the spectrum of the corresponding wave operator is fully determined by zeroes of an entire function. Consequently, a considerable change of spectral properties is shown for certain critical values of the damping parameter. We also derive a definitive criterion for the Riesz basis property of the root vectors for an arbitrary placement of a complex-valued Dirac damping. Finally, we consider a generalisation of the problem for compact star graphs and provide insight into the essence of the critical damping constant.

papers.title: Galerkin Approximation of the Fractional Sobolev Constant
papers.abstract: We establish sharp estimates for the discrete optimal constant of the fractional Sobolev inequality in dimension $N\geq 1$, with fractional exponent $s\in (0,\min\{1,N/2\})$. The convergence rates that we establish take place for the Galerkin approximation with piecewise linear elements, when the problem is posed in the unit ball, for which we employ a quasi-uniform and regular mesh. Since the infimum defining the fractional Sobolev constant is not attained on bounded domains, these estimates quantify how far a piecewise affine mesh of size $h$ can resolve the concentration of the optimizers: the discrete minimizers are close to bubbles concentrated at the scale $h^{2(2-s)/(N+4(1-s))}$, and the energy gap is exactly of order $h^{2(2-s)(N-2s)/(N+4(1-s))}$.

papers.title: Bregman-projected mirror methods for regularized stationary mean-field games
papers.authors: Hussain Al Abdulaziz, Yuri Ashrafyan, Yeva Gevorgyan, Diogo Gomes
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze a Bregman-projected mirror iteration for low-order regularizations of stationary mean-field game (MFG) systems in their natural Banach space setting. For separable Hamiltonians of the form $H(x,p,m)=H_0(x,p)-g(m)$, with quadratic or super-quadratic Hamiltonian growth and linear or super-linear density couplings, we formulate a low-order $\bar\gamma$-Laplacian regularization of the stationary MFG system as a variational inequality on $L^{\bar\beta}(\mathbb T^d)\times W^{1,\bar\gamma}(\mathbb T^d)$. To approximate solutions of this regularized variational inequality, we introduce a Bregman geometry matched to the mixed Lebesgue-Sobolev exponents of the problem and analyze the exact constrained one-step mirror iteration and a frozen two-step variant. Under quantitative monotonicity of the coupling, both exact iterations converge strongly to the unique solution of the regularized variational inequality for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, under natural summability conditions on the step sizes. Along weakly convergent vanishing-regularization sequences, we also prove strong convergence in the full product space. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions show first-order accuracy on manufactured solutions and weak dependence of outer iteration counts on the tested grids. At matched effective step sizes, the frozen two-step and one-step implementations agree up to inner-solve accuracy, while the latter requires fewer mirror solves.

papers.title: Searching Schemes With $p$-Adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems
papers.abstract: Firstly, for branched covering maps $f\colon Y\to X$ between smooth, separated schemes of finite type over the integral ring $O_K$ of a non-archimedean local field $K$, the ramification divisor is found to coincide with the divisor of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the Radon measure associated with an algebraic differential form on $Y$ against the pullback measure of one on $X$, both taking Borel sets of the space $Y(O_K)$ of $O_K$-rational points of $Y$ as input values. Secondly, the ultracontractivity of semigroups generated by Laplacian integral operators having a geodetic-distance-power kernel function is proven, using heat kernel estimates for ultrametric operators on $p$-adic balls. Thirdly, a series of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems, depending on algebraic and pluricanonical differential forms with poles on spaces $X(O_K)$ coming from schemes is formulated and solved, extending previous work of the author. These results are then used to solve reconstruction problems on schemes: the divisor of a pluricanonical form with poles with at worst log-terminal singularities, as well as Weierstrass points of projective algebraic curves can be reconstructed via repeatedly finding weak solutions of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems.

papers.title: An Atiyah-Segal homomorphism for approximate representations of infinite groups, and almost multiplicative ucp maps
papers.abstract:
The Atiyah-Segal homomorphism relates the representation ring of a finite group to the $K$-theory ring of its classifying space. We develop a version of this for infinite groups, but based on a ring of approximate representations rather than representations. We then use known results on the Baum-Connes conjecture to show that our homomorphism is an isomorphism for many groups: this includes all torsion-free amenable groups, and all torsion-free fundamental groups of compact manifolds of dimension at most three. The main motivation is the desire to understand approximate representations using topological tools: as a sample application we give some examples of torsion phenomena in approximate representation theory.
  The methods of proof are $C^*$-algebraic: the key idea is to relate our Atiyah-Segal type homomorphism to Kasparov's coassembly map. The main step realizes (Hausdorffized) $KK$-theory as approximately multiplicative ucp maps modulo stable approximate unitary equivalence for appropriate $C^*$-algebras. This is in the spirit of the stable uniqueness theorems of Dadarlat-Eilers and Lin, and may be of purely $C^*$-algebraic interest.

papers.title: An explicit Dennis trace and its compatibility with Koszul duality
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct explicit Dennis trace maps from algebraic $K$-theory to Hochschild homology for dg module and curved dg comodule categories, and prove their compatibility with derived Koszul duality. For this, we construct a natural chain map $\tau$ from the chains on the newly defined thickened nerve to the total complex of the dg cyclic nerve, with explicit formulas incorporating morphisms and coherent higher homotopies, which generalizes McCarthy's approach. This $\tau$ construction works both for modules over dg algebras and for cdg comodules over counital conilpotent curved dg coalgebras. Combining the $\tau$ with the dg-enriched Waldhausen $S_\bullet$-construction and a Hochschild delooping theorem yields the Dennis trace maps. For thick subcategories corresponding under derived Koszul duality, we prove that the induced $K$-theory equivalences and Hochschild homology isomorphisms fit into natural commutative diagrams with these trace maps.

papers.title: Additive invariants of Finite-dimensional DG-algebras
papers.abstract: Orlov has shown that additive invariants such as K-theory and Hochschild homology of smooth finite-dimensional DG-algebras behave similarly to those of finite-dimensional algebras. The similarities only go so far: there are examples of finite-dimensional DG-algebras with vanishing and uncountable Grothendieck groups. We show that for DG-quivers with relations, the Grothendieck groups are free of the expected rank and that, in the smooth case, all additive invariants are determined by the base field. We use our results to rule out certain finite-dimensional DG-algebras from being phantoms.

papers.title: Twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes and the rational hit conjecture
papers.abstract: We study the top degree concentration property for the cohomology of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes of multiarrangements of hyperplanes. Our main tool is a short exact sequence of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes based on the deletion-restriction exact sequences for logarithmic differential forms found recently by Abe and Denham. We prove a number of general results that can be used to establish the top degree cohomology concentration property, and also establish that property for some families of multiarrangements. As a consequence of our results, we prove the rational hit conjecture of R.~M.~W.~Wood about the coinvariants of the rational Steenrod algebra acting on the polynomial ring. We also make progress on the deformed version of that conjecture proposed by Hivert and Thi\'ery, prove generalizations of the rational hit conjecture for all complex reflection groups $G(m,p,n)$, thus answering questions of Bergeron, Borie and Thi\'ery, and generalize the rational hit conjecture to all standard subalgebras of the rational Steenrod algebra.

papers.title: $\mathbb{C}$-Motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane Spectra as $\mathrm{MGL}$-Motivic Thom Spectra and Normed $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology
papers.abstract: We exhibit the $p$-complete $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_p$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_p^{\wedge}$ as $\mathbb{E_3}$-$\mathrm{MGL}_p^{\wedge}$-motivic Thom spectra over the motivic $\mathbb{G}_m$-loop spaces $\Omega_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BGL}$ and $\Omega_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BSL}$, respectively. Furthermore, for $p=2$, we compute the $\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}$-relative $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology $\mathbb{G}_m \odot^{\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}} {-}$, recently introduced by Bachmann-Burklund-Dundas-{\O}stv{\ae}r, of $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$ to be $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{BGL}]$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}[\mathrm{BSL}]$ as $\mathbb{E}_2$-$\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$-algebras and $\mathbb{E}_2$-$(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$-algebras, respectively.

papers.title: Splitting vector bundles over real algebraic varieties
papers.authors: Aravind Asok, Jean Fasel, Samuel Lerbet
papers.abstract:
Suppose $X$ is a smooth affine real variety and $\mathscr{E}$ is a vector bundle over $X$. We analyze the problem of splitting off a free rank one summand from $\mathscr{E}$ in corank $0$ and $1$. The problem in corank $0$ can be viewed as the search for a real analog of Murthy's celebrating splitting theorem in the algebraically closed case: to wit, beyond the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory, are the obstructions to splitting ``purely topological''? In a sense, the answer in this case is yes, and we give a proof, using motivic techniques, of a mild extension of the results of Bhatwadekar-Sridharan and Bhatwadekar-Das-Mandal.
  In corank $1$, in the algebraically closed situation, Murthy's splitting conjecture (now a theorem in characteristic $0$) predicts that the vanishing of the top Chern class in Chow theory is the only obstruction to splitting off a free rank $1$ summand, and we can search for a suitable ``real'' analog of this assertion. We observe that several natural guesses for a ``real'' analog of Murthy's splitting conjecture cannot be true, i.e., that the situation over the real numbers is rather complicated.

papers.title: Equivalence of categories of bivariant K-theory for C*-algebras over topological spaces via reflection functors
papers.abstract: In this paper, for various pairs of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$, we introduce an analogue of the Bern\v{s}te\u{\i}n-Gel'fand-Ponomarev reflection functors between the categories of C*-algebras over $X$ and $Y$. We prove that these functors induce equivalences $\mathfrak{KK}(X)_{\mathrm{loc}} \simeq \mathfrak{KK}(Y)_{\mathrm{loc}}$ between Meyer and Nest's localizing subcategories in Kirchberg's ideal-related KK-theory, and $\mathfrak{E}(X) \simeq \mathfrak{E}(Y)$ between the entire categories in Dadarlat and Meyer's ideal-related E-theory. Both equivalences restrict to the respective bootstrap categories: $\mathcal{B}(X) \simeq \mathcal{B}(Y)$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{E}}(X) \simeq \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{E}}(Y)$. Combining these equivalences with a combinatorial argument in quiver representation theory, we obtain the same equivalences for any two finite $T_0$-spaces whose Hasse diagrams are orientations of the same tree. Moreover, we prove a rearrangement property of reflection functors, which yields an analogue of Coxeter functors. Finally, we apply reflection functors to give a conceptual alternative proof of Bentmann and K\"ohler's universal coefficient theorem for filtrated K-theory over finite $T_0$-spaces whose Hasse diagrams are orientations of Dynkin diagrams of type A.

papers.title: Singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type and standard eventually homological isomorphisms
papers.authors: Yang Han, Yongyun Qin, Xianqing Wang
papers.abstract: We refine the definition of eventually homological isomorphisms so that it becomes more natural and fruitful. We introduce singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type which can be viewed as standard singular equivalences of different levels and are more convenient for reducing various homological conjectures and transferring homological properties. We develop the theories of singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type for $n\ge 2$ and standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories by giving their characterizations in terms of $\otimes$-(co)perfect complexes of bimodules, two constructions via opposite algebras and tensor product algebras, examples induced by homomorphisms of algebras and idempotents, and applications to the reduction of homological conjectures such as the finitistic dimension conjecture, Gorenstein symmetry conjecture and Auslander-Reiten conjecture, as well as to the preservation of homological properties such as Gorensteinness, the Fg condition, Happel's property and Han's property. Moreover, we show that essentially surjective standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories correspond to standard singular equivalences with canonical left adjoint.

papers.title: BV rigidity for compact Lie groups and the integral string topology of the symplectic group
papers.authors: Mukilraj K (Indian Institute of Science Education,Research Kolkata, India)
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected compact Lie group and $R$ a commutative ring over which $H_*(G;R)$ is an exterior algebra on odd primitive generators. We prove a rigidity theorem: the Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ of Chas and Sullivan on the homology of the free loop space is that of the product of odd spheres with the classical exponents of $G$, tensored with the group ring of the torsion of $\pi_1(G)$. Conversely, over an integral domain the graded algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ already determines the exponents and the group ring, hence the BV algebra. If moreover $G$ is simply connected, then $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$, as a BV algebra, is the Hochschild cohomology of $H^*(G;R)$ with the BV operator induced by Poincar\'e duality. The isomorphism with the product of spheres is algebraic: for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, $n\geq2$, and $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $n\geq3$, no map of spaces induces it over $\mathbb{Z}$. We compute, in Hepworth's presentation, the integral BV algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(L\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})$ with its Gerstenhaber bracket, open for $n\geq2$, the running example of the rigidity theorem.

papers.title: T-embeddings as stationary measures on T-graphs
papers.authors: Mikhail Basok, Benoit Laslier, Marianna Russkikh
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the relation between t-embeddings and T-graphs associated with the same weighted planar bipartite graph. We prove that, given such a T-graph, the corresponding t-embeddings are classified by positive stationary measures on this T-graph and describe a reconstruction procedure of the t-embedding given such a measure. As an application, we develop an approach for constructing t-embeddings of arbitrary sufficiently non-degenerate planar bipartite graphs.

papers.title: An Accurate Zeroth-Order Perturbation Theory for Solving Power-Law Potentials within the Framework of the Asymptotic Iteration Method
papers.authors: A. J. Sous, Ibsal Assi, Nasser Saad
papers.abstract: Spherically symmetric singular potentials have a wide range of applications, such as molecular and atomic physics. In this work, we present a zeroth-order perturbation theory for solving the Schr\"odinger equation within the framework of the asymptotic iteration method (AIM). We rely on exponential and hyperbolic potential ansatz substitutions, where the difference between the original and new potential is treated as a small perturbation. Each potential ansatz has a free parameter chosen small enough to give an accurate zeroth-order perturbative wave equation solution. This method avoids the oscillatory behavior observed in the asymptotic iteration solutions when applying the AIM to such problems. Finally, we illustrate our approach by solving a few problems, particularly potentials with quartic and sextic singularities. We compare our results with those obtained via other methods and find good agreement.

papers.title: Eynard-Orantin Topological Recursion, Moduli-Space Virasoro Constraints, and Semisimple CohFTs
papers.abstract: We use Virasoro constraints to prove Eynard's intersection-number formula for Eynard-Orantin topological recursion with several simple ramification points. The key construction couples the higher Weil-Petersson partition functions associated with the individual ramification points through a quadratic differential operator determined by the Bergman kernel. We identify this operator with the quadratic part of Givental's quantized $R$-matrix, thereby obtaining a Virasoro-theoretic proof of the DOSS identification of topological recursion with Givental's formula for semisimple cohomological field theories. Furthermore, while the DOSS identification fixes the distinguished $y$-function, we keep the Bergman kernel/$R$-matrix fixed and allow $y$ to vary, showing that this amounts to shifting the evaluation point of the corresponding ancestor potential.

papers.title: Spectral Curves for Semisimple Conformal Frobenius Manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct connected spectral curves for semisimple conformal Frobenius manifolds with flat unit, using the periods of the second structure equation. Eynard-Orantin topological recursion on these curves reproduces the stable ancestor correlators of Givental-Teleman reconstruction. The spectral curves are defined on simply connected domains in the complex plane. We apply the construction to the quantum cohomology of $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\ge2$ at a point, obtaining explicit spectral curve data in terms of Hecke triangle groups and hypergeometric functions. Finally, for $\mathbb P^2$ and $\mathbb P^3$, we express the complete spectral curve data, including the bidifferentials, in classical modular and quasimodular forms.

papers.title: Thoughts on Quantum Events, Quantizing Gravity and von Neumann Algebras
papers.abstract: This short document presents no new results. It is a collection of related ideas that may lead to a way of quantizing gravity. To achieve this it may be relevant to use my recent new approach to quantum theory, which is based on quantum events. Given that most standard quantum texts do not define a mathematical object which corresponds to a physical event, the definition of a quantum event is motivated and discussed in detail. This in turn leads to the idea that the mathematical object that contains enough quantum events for describing a quantum system is a von Neumann algebra. The next idea is that the kinematics of special relativity (as embodied in flat Minkowski space) should be quantized as a first step in the program of the quantization of general relativity, that is, quantizing Einstein's equation. It must be emphasized that the events of special relativity are viewed as part of the kinematics, rather than of the dynamics of that theory. The same holds for general relativity. Similarly, I am viewing quantum events as part of the kinematics of quantum theory, even though some find this to be counterintuitive. An Appendix shows how ``collapse'' is easily understood in this new approach to quantum theory.

papers.title: Complementary Cauchy Elasticity
papers.abstract: We develop a nonlinear theory of complementary Cauchy elasticity in which the right Cauchy-Green strain is prescribed as a function of the second Piola-Kirchhoff stress, without assuming constitutive invertibility or the existence of a complementary strain-energy function. We introduce the complementary stress-work 1-form and characterize the obstruction to complementary hyperelasticity through the failure of major symmetry of the tangent compliance tensor. For general implicit elasticity, we show that the simultaneous closure of the stress-work and complementary stress-work 1-forms is characterized by the Lagrangian structure of the constitutive manifold. Using the Darboux classification, we obtain local canonical representations of anisotropic and isotropic complementary Cauchy elastic solids, including explicit non-hyperelastic examples. We investigate kinematic and stress constraints, including applications to pentamode solids, and show that internally constrained constitutive relations are naturally formulated on equivalence classes of stresses modulo reactive stresses. We formulate the balance laws and thermodynamics covariantly and establish that covariance of the energy balance directly yields the balance of angular momentum in complementary Cauchy elasticity, unlike in conventional Cauchy elasticity. Finally, we linearize implicit, Cauchy, and complementary Cauchy elasticity about finitely deformed and prestressed configurations and show that nonlinear non-hyperelastic solids may possess hyperelastic linearized responses.

papers.title: Response theory at low temperature for weakly interacting quantum spin systems
papers.authors: Joscha Henheik, Marius Lemm, Tom Wessel
papers.abstract: Recent work by Greenblatt, Lange, Marcelli, and Porta (Commun. Math. Phys. 2024) provides the first rigorous justification of adiabatic theory for interacting quantum systems at positive temperature. Their analysis treats weakly interacting lattice fermions and combines a rigorous Wick rotation with fermionic cluster expansion techniques. Here, we study a class of weakly interacting quantum spin systems and derive response theory at positive temperature, thereby covering non-Fermi systems for the first time. Our proof identifies and exploits the locality property of local indistinguishability as a key ingredient in carrying out low-temperature adiabatic expansions. The fact that these systems satisfy local indistinguishability was recently established jointly with Adhikari (arXiv:2508.15907) using cluster expansion methods together with a probabilistic swapping trick.

papers.title: Upper Bound on the Correlation Energy of a Dense Fermi Gas in the Thermodynamic Limit
papers.authors: Niels Benedikter, Sascha Lill, Marcello Porta, Benjamin Schlein
papers.abstract: We prove that the random phase approximation provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density. More precisely, we consider a mean-field scaling regime where the kinetic and interaction Hamiltonian are scaled by $\rho^{-2/3}$ and $\rho^{-1}$, respectively. We use a correlated trial state constructed through a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle--hole excitations associated to patches on the Fermi surface. Key of the proof is to control the position-space localization of the collective excitations. Combined with an iterated Duhamel expansion of the expectation values of (localized) particle number operators we obtain extensive estimates, which justify the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian and its approximate diagonalization.

papers.title: De Finetti Structures in Networks of Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Consider $N$ identical quantum systems at the vertices of a graph, interacting via pairwise edge couplings. We designate $K$ vertices as a system of interest $\mathrm S$ and the remaining $N-K$ as a reservoir $\mathrm R$. Under generic connectivity assumptions between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$, we show that for $N\to\infty$, the reduced state of $\mathrm S$ converges to a convex combination of symmetric product states of $K$ single-vertex density matrices -- called a de Finetti representation. Unlike in standard derivations for symmetric (exchangeable) systems, we establish de Finetti representations for quantum networks, which are inherently non-exchangeable. We construct the representations explicitly and quantify the convergence rate. We show that Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graphs exhibit the de Finetti structure: as the reservoir grows, the reduced state of any fixed finite subgraph converges almost surely to an explicit deterministic product state. As applications, we establish a general area law for the entanglement entropy of $\mathrm S$, analyze mean-field and fluctuation scalings of the $\mathrm S$-$\mathrm R$ interaction, and illustrate our results on qubit networks. We also derive quantitative convergence estimates for information-theoretic quantities, including von Neumann entropy, mutual information, and entanglement within $\mathrm S$ and between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$.

papers.title: Symmetry algebra of a charged harmonic oscillator in the field of the Dirac magnetic monopole
papers.abstract: A charged particle bound by an isotropic harmonic potential to a Dirac magnetic monopole, with the centrifugal term that makes the orbits close, has degeneracies beyond rotational invariance: for integer $q$, the product of the electric and magnetic charges, the levels are those of the oscillator with the states of angular momentum $l<|q|$ removed. The conserved rank-2 tensor $T$ built from the ladder operators that accounts for them was identified thirty-five years ago, but the algebra it generates with the angular momentum $\mathbf{J}$ was not obtained. We obtain its relations in covariant form and identify it. It is polynomial but not quadratic, and the shift $T'=T+2(H-1)J^{(2)}$ by the quadrupole of $\mathbf{J}$, and only this one, makes all commutators polynomials in $\mathbf{J}$. In each sector of fixed energy and $J_z$, $(\mathbf{J}^2,T'_{zz})$ generates a cubic algebra of Heun--Racah type whose parameters are symmetric, up to a scalar shift, in the magnetic charge and the magnetic quantum number. At $q=0$, $T$ is the algebraic Heun operator of the pair (Casimir of $\mathfrak{so}(3)$, quadrupole of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$): the symmetry algebra is the $\mathfrak{so}(3)$-covariant extension of a Heun--Racah algebra. We define it abstractly and classify its multiplicity-free finite-dimensional representations at the energies of the system: besides the levels, they include, for nonzero integer $q$, a second family carried by the states the monopole removes, the kernel of the Newman--Penrose operator. All relations are derived from the dynamical algebra of the ladder operators and hold for integer and half-integer charges alike.

papers.title: Upper bounds on the number of images produced by point-mass lenses at different distances
