In particular, we characterize explicit logical representatives of the full gauged code space, and provide a fundamental treatment of non-Abelian code distance in the sense of Knill--Laflamme based on combining expansion with cleaning to establish protection against arbitrary errors. We further construct an almost-good family with entire code spaces exhibiting long-range magic. Moreover, we use linearly addressable cup product to directly generate linearly many encoded magic states from gauging measurements of Clifford operators. These results extend good qLDPC codes beyond the Pauli stabilizer setting, lay the foundation for pursuing the no low-energy trivial magic conjecture and shed light on non-Abelian quantum phases and orders beyond geometric locality.

papers.title: A Hopf Algebraic Theory of the Quantum Magnusian
papers.authors: Li Guo, Joon-Hwi Kim, Jung-Wook Kim, Sungsoo Kim, Sangmin Lee, Jian-Rong Li
papers.abstract:
We develop a Hopf-algebraic theory of graph coefficients arising in the quantum Magnus expansion. At the classical level, the expansion is governed by directed trees, whereas its quantum counterpart involves loop graphs, multiple edges, and several types of edge data. We introduce a contraction Hopf algebra of mixed quivers containing these diagrams and closed under contraction.
  On this algebra we define a character $e$ from normalized linear-extension data, directed-tadpole factors, and a prescription for undirected edges, and let $\omega$ be its convolution inverse. Our main result is a universal closed formula for the connected function $\omega_c$ on every finite mixed quiver, expressed as a finite sum over ordered set partitions of the vertices. We also construct a weighted vertex-splitting Hopf structure on the unlocalized mixed-quiver algebra, with convolution $\star_V$ and canonical edge-weight character $\zeta_V$, such that $\omega_c=\log_{\star_V}\zeta_V$. Compatibility of the two coproducts and an explicit identity between their characters explain this equality. We further prove that the two-vertex contraction identity, tadpole factorization, vanishing on disconnected graphs, and boundary data uniquely determine $\omega_c$.
  For acyclic quivers, the formula reduces to a permutation formula with coefficients depending only on descent numbers. We derive this formula independently from the quantum Magnus expansion using operator products and Wick contractions, showing that the physical graph coefficients are governed by the convolution structure of the contraction Hopf algebra. Further consequences include a refined quantum Murua formula and orientation-sum identities related to Tutte and chromatic polynomials.

papers.title: The Riemann theta function near soliton limit
papers.abstract: It has been known that (the square of) Jacobi elliptic function can be expressed by an infinite sum of single solitons of $\sech^2$ shape. In this paper, we show that there exists a similar structure for higher genus cases. It turns out that this is just a consequence of the quasi-periodicity of the Riemann $\theta$-function. More precisely, we show that the second derivative of $\log \theta$ with the \emph{real} Riemann $\theta$-function of genus $g$ near soliton limit can be well approximated by the \emph{sum} of \emph{real} and \emph{regular} $g$-soliton solutions of Hirota-type in $g$-dimensional real space $\R^g$. This leads to a tessellation of $\R^g$, whose tile is an oblique prism divided into $2^g$ sections by hyper-planes of dominant exponents in the theta function. We apply the results to study quasi-periodic solutions to the KdV and KP equations. We construct the quasi-periodic solutions using the Schottky group, which uniformizes the corresponding Riemann surfaces. We also discuss solitons on quasi-periodic background by pinching some of the homological cycles

papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and combine local boundary analysis with a global argument on an algebraic curve. We exclude Diagrams~1, 2, 4, 6 and~8 for complex germs, Diagram~7 on curves through real configurations, and Diagram~3 on curves with a positive arc. For Diagrams~5 and~9, direct order estimates show that the product $\Delta$ of all squared mutual distances tends to zero. On a hypothetical curve containing a positive arc, a first pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $\Delta$. On the completed curve, $\Delta$ must then have a pole elsewhere. The identity $\Delta^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$ forces a four-product to have a pole there, contradicting the same vanishing conclusion. The computer-assisted inputs concern Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 and use exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.

papers.title: Separation of variables for coupled radiative perturbations of Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes
papers.abstract: We extend Hintz's separation of variables for radiative gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations from Kerr-Newman to Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes. On subextremal backgrounds with nonzero rotation and charge, an explicit algebraic matrix transformation yields coupled two-component radial and angular ordinary differential systems linked by a common separation constant. The transformation is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both signs of spin weight. For real frequencies, we establish a complete angular mode decomposition. We also translate regularity at the future black hole outer and cosmological horizons into ingoing and outgoing boundary conditions, respectively, for the separated radial systems. These results show that exact separation of the coupled radiative equations extends beyond asymptotically flat Kerr-Newman spacetime.

papers.title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
papers.authors: Yifan Wang, Josip Tambaca, Suncica Canic
papers.abstract:
We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes.
  We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.
